title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE NATIONAL SARAS MELA IN VIJAYAWADA
subtitle: SHGs AND SARAS MELAS CAN PLAY A LEADING ROLE IN EXTENDING THE BENEFITS OF DEVELOPMENT TO EVERY VILLAGE AND EVERY HOUSEHOLD: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the National SARAS Mela, organised by the Union Ministry of Rural Development and the Government of Andhra Pradesh, in Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh today (October 15, 2026). The President also visited the SARAS stalls and interacted with Lakhpati Didis on the occasion.
Addressing the gathering, the President said that rural women play a vital role in agriculture. Through Self-Help Groups, they have found a new path to financial, technical, and social empowerment. She was happy to note that along with an encouraging rise in women's entrepreneurship, rural women's participation in economic decision-making has also increased. She said that it is essential for equitable and inclusive development of our country.
The President noted that Women's Self-Help Groups have contributed effectively to the rural economy. Over the last 12 years, the number of women associated with these groups has risen to more than 10 crores. These women are connected to over 90 lakh Self-Help Groups. She highlighted that they are making a meaningful contribution to the economic well-being of their families. She said that this process of participation is contributing to women-centric, inclusive rural development. It has also led to a vast expansion of opportunities for collective enterprise.
The President was happy to note that Women's Self-Help Groups are playing an important role in community activities and SHGs are making significant contributions to the holistic transformation of rural life and inclusive development of our country.
The President said that the Government of India has imparted a distinct momentum and direction to rural women's empowerment through the 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative. Increasing participation in various modern sectors such as digital services and renewable energy has opened up new avenues for skill development for rural women.
The President said that today, rural women are not merely beneficiaries of schemes. They have become wealth creators and are emerging as drivers of development. Yet, we still have a long way to go on this journey of empowerment. A key yardstick for empowerment should be the extent to which rural women have gained control over their own income and assets. At the same time, there is a need to promote community-based support systems for domestic care responsibilities. Rural women's participation in climate-resilient enterprises must also be increased.
The President said that SARAS Melas are evolving into platforms for strengthening the rural economy. These fairs have been established as thriving rural markets. Through them, the direct connection between rural women entrepreneurs and consumers across the country has been strengthened. She said that to achieve the goal of Viksit Bharat by 2047, it is essential to extend the benefits of development to every village and every household. SHGs and SARAS Melas can play a leading role in this endeavour.
Around 1500 women SHG entrepreneurs and Lakhpati Didis from 34 States and Union Territories are showcasing their products through more than 650 stalls in this edition of the National SARAS Mela, which is open till October 31, 2026.

content:

Radhakrishnan, today called for greater scientific research into Ayurveda to establish the efficacy of traditional healthcare practices, strengthen patient confidence and enhance the global acceptance of India’s traditional systems of medicine. Congratulating AIIA on its 10th Foundation Day, he emphasised the importance of sustained efforts in research, innovation and academic excellence to further strengthen the Institute’s standing.

He highlighted the establishment of a separate Ministry of AYUSH in 2014 and its efforts to strengthen education, expand healthcare services and promote scientific research. title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacts with the contingent of Indian athletes who participated in Asian Games 2026
subtitle:
Our Asian Games champions have made the Tricolour fly high and enhanced its honour and pride: PM

The pride of the Tricolour in every arena, India’s new identity in sports, New champions in every sport, And new records in our name; We will do it: PM

India is all set to become a global sporting powerhouse: PM
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with the Indian contingent that participated in the Asian Games 2026 today. He remarked on the wonderful atmosphere created by gathering with so many medal-winners in one place. "All of you young athletes are examples of how when passion turns into victory, it brings a glow to faces along with medals,” remarked Shri Modi.
Praising the athletes for bringing immense pride to 140 crore citizens, the Prime Minister emphasized that the ultimate achievement lies in elevating the honor and glory of the national flag. He congratulated the players, their coaches, support staff, and families for this collective national triumph. "Therefore, your success is not yours alone; it is also the success of crores of citizens of the country,” affirmed PM Modi.
Remembering former President Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam on his birth anniversary, the Prime Minister paid rich tributes to the late statesman. He highlighted how Dr. Kalam's remarkable life and visionary outlook continue to guide the nation. "His life and his vision are an inspiration for all of us,” remarked Shri Modi.
Recalling the historic milestones achieved at the Asian Games, the Prime Minister celebrated the double Gold victory of the men's and women's hockey teams, with the women ending a 44-year wait, alongside consecutive medals for both cricket teams and dual Golds in Kabaddi. He also lauded the five Golds in archery, stellar displays in shooting, boxing, and wrestling, new athletics records, a weightlifting medal after 28 years, and the first marathon success since 1982. "This time the Asian Games have been memorable for us in many ways,” noted PM Modi.
Applauding the extraordinary contribution of female athletes who secured 38 of India's 85 total medals, including 11 Golds, the Prime Minister stated that their tally represents far more than mere statistics and reflects an empowered New India. He also highlighted how Indian players scripted history by winning maiden Asian Games medals in disciplines like mixed martial arts, soft tennis, and specific sailing events. "Today India is winning medals even in those sports in which we had never won a medal in the history of the Asian Games before,” observed Shri Modi.
Calling upon the athletes to scale even greater heights in the sporting arena, the Prime Minister led an energetic pledge where the contingent chanted "We will Do it!" in unison. He rallied them to uphold the Tricolor's glory on every field, forge a new sporting identity for the nation, and create new champions across every discipline. "More new records in our name, We will do it!” asserted PM Modi.
Drawing attention to the venue of the gathering, the Prime Minister reminded the athletes that the stadium is named after the legendary Major Dhyan Chand, who famously practiced hockey for hours into the night. He pointed to the icon's relentless dedication to illustrate that grand resolutions require years of sustained patience and hard work. "This hard work of his reminds us time and again that resolutions and dreams are not fulfilled in a single day,” remarked Shri Modi.
Contrasting the past dozen years of diligent work on the sports ecosystem with an earlier era when India won only a handful of medals and remained unaware of many disciplines, the Prime Minister recalled how the nation previously had zero representation in over half the Olympic events. He questioned how the country could ever expect to win laurels without first stepping onto the field of competition. "If we do not even compete, how will we bring medals?” remarked PM Modi.
Highlighting a decisive shift in national sporting policy, the Prime Minister emphasized the government's firm determination to eradicate this historic apathy and self-doubt. He celebrated the resulting surge in Indian athletes competing across international arenas today. "We took this resolution that we will remove this pessimistic mindset!” asserted Shri Modi.
Attributing this transformation to a far-reaching vision and sincere effort over the last 10 to 12 years, the Prime Minister detailed the creation of a transparent, modern sports ecosystem anchored by the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS) and the expanded Khelo India initiative. He pointed out that the government has committed massive financial resources to strengthen sports federations and grassroots programs across the country. "To expand Khelo India and strengthen sports federations, more than 36 thousand crore rupees were allocated,” noted PM Modi.
Detailing the rapid expansion of grassroots infrastructure across over a thousand Khelo India Centers, the Prime Minister listed thousands of new stadiums, multi-purpose halls, athletics tracks, football and hockey grounds, and swimming pools being built across cities of all sizes. He also highlighted direct financial support to athletes, including a 50,000-rupee monthly Out-of-Pocket Allowance under TOPS and funding for international coaching stints. "If there is a need to go outside the country for coaching in any sport, the government is facilitating that too and providing financial assistance for it,” observed Shri Modi.
Underscoring the drive to maximize competitive exposure through the Winter Games, Sansad Khel Pratiyogitas, and the new 'Khelo Bharat Niti', the Prime Minister also praised Divyang athletes for bringing laurels to the nation. He noted that the athletes' own triumphs prove what happens when players know the entire nation backs their journey. "Today every player has this confidence that the country stands with them throughout their entire journey,” affirmed PM Modi.
Spotlighting the remarkable performances of 15-to-17-year-old athletes in the contingent as proof that starting young provides an added advantage, the Prime Minister outlined a targeted focus on identifying and training children aged five to fifteen through Khelo India and Emerging Khelo India. Looking ahead to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, India's hosting of the 2030 Commonwealth Games, and the aspiration to host the 2036 Olympics, he recalled his Red Fort announcement of a nationwide village-level talent hunt. "These very players will bring medals for India in the times to come,” asserted Shri Modi.
Expressing unwavering confidence in the nation's grand resolutions, the Prime Minister led another spirited "We will Do it!" chant with the athletes. He rallied them around the shared goals of hosting major global sporting events, joining the ranks of top sporting nations, building world-class infrastructure, and becoming a global sports hub. "A champion from every corner of India, We will do it!” asserted PM Modi.
Connecting the Asian Games triumph to the broader aspirations of Indian youth, the Prime Minister noted how young innovators have propelled India into the world's third-largest startup ecosystem while pioneering breakthroughs in space, satellite technology, defense, and Artificial Intelligence. He emphasized that just like in sports, youth from small towns and villages are driving this entrepreneurial wave, backed by a decade of systemic reforms that assure them of the nation's full support. "They have the trust that to take their dreams forward, the entire capability of the country stands with them,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Expanding on the broader economic impact of the sporting boom, the Prime Minister pointed out that government initiatives are benefiting far more than just on-field competitors. He highlighted the rapid emergence of diverse professional fields such as sports coaching, physiotherapy, sports management, and sports broadcasting. "This has created new avenues of employment and enterprise for the youth,” noted PM Modi.
Urging the internationally experienced medalists to shoulder the responsibility of mentoring the next generation, the Prime Minister asked them to visit schools, return to their original playing grounds, and engage with children in their home villages and cities. He emphasized that sharing their hard-earned experiences could profoundly inspire young aspirants dreaming of following in their footsteps. "Perhaps, a small word from you might give a child the courage to move ahead in sports,” remarked Shri Modi.
Reflecting on the deeper value of athletics beyond the playing field, the Prime Minister stated that sports instill lifelong discipline, adaptability, steadfastness toward long-term goals, and the resilience to rise after a defeat. He noted that these foundational qualities naturally integrate into daily life to guide individuals through every challenge. "This very sportsperson spirit comes in handy throughout life,” observed PM Modi.
Concluding his address with his signature maxim that "one who plays, will flourish," the Prime Minister praised the athletes' enthusiasm as New India's greatest strength and led a final "We will Do it!" chant encompassing the goals of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, a top-three economy, an Aatmanirbhar Bharat, a global manufacturing hub, technology leadership, space exploration, and hosting the Olympics. He extended his best wishes for all their future tournaments and endeavors. "With this very self-confidence, we have to take India to new heights,” asserted Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM’s address during interaction with the participants of Asian Games 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 7:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Sports Shri Mansukh Mandaviya ji, Minister of State for Sports Sister Raksha Khadse ji, all of you young athletes, coaches, other distinguished guests, ladies and gentlemen.
Coming among all of you fills me with energy as well. So many medal winners gathered together, and meeting all of them at once, is no ordinary thing. It is a very pleasant feeling. All of you young athletes are examples of how, when passion is transformed into victory, it brings not only medals but also a glow on the face. And, of course, it makes the nation shine as well.
Friends,
You have given 1.4 billion countrymen an opportunity to feel proud. Because the greatest achievement, if there is one, is to enhance the honour of the Tiranga. You have enhanced the pride of the Tiranga, you have increased its honour. Therefore, your success is not yours alone; it is the success of millions and millions of citizens of this country. On behalf of all the people of India, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you. At the same time, I also wholeheartedly congratulate your coaches, your support staff, and your families.
Friends,
Today is also the birth anniversary of our former President, Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam. His life and his vision are an inspiration to all of us. I respectfully pay tribute to him as well.
Friends,
In many ways, these Asian Games have been memorable for us. Both our men’s and women’s hockey teams are present here today. Both teams won gold medals this time. And especially our women’s hockey team, you ended a long wait of 44 years by bringing home the gold medal. In cricket, both our teams won medals for the second consecutive time and, in fact, repeated their own record. In kabaddi too, both our men’s and women’s teams won gold medals. Likewise, five gold medals in archery, and where there are five, there is the grace of the Almighty. Outstanding performances in shooting, major successes in boxing and wrestling, new records in athletics, a medal in weightlifting after twenty-eight years, and India’s success in marathon events for the first time since 1982. All this is truly a matter of great joy.
Friends,
I especially want to appreciate our daughters. Out of the 85 medals won by India, 38 medals were won by our women athletes. Among them were 11 gold medals as well. And these medals are not merely numbers; they represent a powerful image of New India. Today, India is winning medals even in sports where, in the history of the Asian Games, we had never before won a medal. In Mixed Martial Arts, Soft Tennis, and certain sailing events, our players created new history by winning medals for the first time.
Friends,
Now we must reach even greater heights in sports. We have to, don't we? We have to achieve even more, don't we? I want to place a few resolutions before you. And all of you must respond with full enthusiasm: We will Do it! So, repeat after me:
The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!
The honour of the Tiranga on every field, We will Do it!
A new identity for India in sports, We will Do it!
New champions in every sport, We will Do it!
More records in our name, We will Do it!
Friends,
The stadium in which we are gathered today is named after Major Dhyan Chand ji. His dedication towards hockey was so great that he would practise for hours even at night. His hard work repeatedly reminds us that resolutions and dreams are not fulfilled in a single day. They require years of patience and sustained effort.
Friends,
Over the past 12 years, India too has worked with great patience and dedication on its sportspersons and its sports ecosystem. There was a time when India could win only a handful of medals in major tournaments. In many sports, people in the country did not even know that such sports existed. There used to be huge events such as the Olympics, yet India had no representation in more than half of the sports. Just think about it. If we do not even compete, then where will the medals come from?
Friends,
We took a pledge that we would remove this pessimistic mindset. And the result is that today, our representation is increasing on every global platform.
Friends,
How did this transformation happen? It happened through the same spirit that helped you achieve success. Over the past 10–12 years, the country worked continuously with dedication and sincerity, pursued a long-term vision, and built a transparent and modern ecosystem for sports. As all of you know, we launched the Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS). We launched the Khelo India Scheme. Over time, its scope was expanded further. As Mansukh Bhai mentioned earlier, more than ₹36,000 crore has been allocated for expanding Khelo India and strengthening sports federations.
Friends,
Today, more than one thousand Khelo India Centres have been established across the country. Stadiums, mini-stadiums, and multi-purpose sports halls have been created. Athletics tracks, football grounds, hockey grounds, swimming pools, and thousands of such sports infrastructures are being built in both small and large cities. Under this scheme, direct assistance is being provided to athletes as well. They are being given Out-of-Pocket Allowances. Under the TOPS scheme, athletes receive ₹50,000 per month. If any sport requires training abroad, the government is facilitating it and providing financial assistance.
Friends,
To ensure that young people get maximum opportunities to play and compete, events such as Winter Games have been launched, and Members of Parliament Sports Competitions have been started. The country created a new Sports Policy and a new Khelo Bharat Policy. Our para-athletes are also enhancing the nation's pride through their talent and capabilities. For them too, better opportunities and modern facilities in sports are being ensured. And that is why every athlete today feels confident that the nation stands beside them throughout their journey. And when an athlete feels that support, what they can achieve for the nation is something all of you yourselves are excellent examples of.
Friends,
This time, many players in Team India at the Asian Games were only 15 to 17 years old. At such a young age, they enhanced the nation’s pride through their outstanding performances. They won the hearts of the people of the country. This shows that age is no barrier to success. In fact, in sports, starting young is an added advantage. That is why our effort is to identify sporting talent from an early age. We are giving special focus to identifying talent among children aged five to fifteen and training them properly. In the coming years, thousands of new athletes will receive opportunities through Khelo India and Emerging Khelo India programmes. We must strengthen our preparations for future sporting events. The Los Angeles Olympics will take place in 2028. India will host the Commonwealth Games in 2030. And hosting the Olympics in 2036 is also India’s aspiration. Keeping this in mind, from the Red Fort I spoke about launching a Talent Hunt campaign. Today, talent is being identified in villages across the country and nurtured. These very athletes will bring medals for India in the years ahead.
Friends,
Our dreams are big. Our resolutions are also big. And today, India has the confidence to achieve them. Every Indian has that confidence. Therefore, with complete conviction, I say:
Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!
Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!
Major sporting events in India, We will Do it!
India among the top sporting nations, We will Do it!
India as a global sports hub, We will Do it!
World-class sports infrastructure in India, We will Do it!
A champion from every corner of India, We will Do it!
Friends,
Our success at the Asian Games is also an example of India’s changing mindset. It shows how today’s youth are impatient to scale every height. There is no summit higher than the determination of India’s youth. There is no goal beyond the capability of our youth power. The limitless sky of possibilities lies before us, and India’s youth are themselves deciding the destination. That is why, in a short span of time, India has become the world’s third-largest startup ecosystem. Our youth are building companies in the space sector. They are working on satellite technology. The same youth are developing new technologies in the defence sector. They are conducting new experiments in Artificial Intelligence. And this transformation is not limited to big cities. Just as talented individuals from remote areas are now getting opportunities in sports, similarly, in startups, research, and other ventures, young people from small cities and villages are coming forward with new ideas. Behind this confidence lies a deep trust. The systems developed by the country over the past decade have given young people confidence that they can dream big. They know that the full strength of the nation stands behind them to help them realise those dreams.
Friends,
The benefits of our efforts are not limited only to athletes who compete on the field. New career opportunities are being created for youth in areas such as sports coaching, physiotherapy, sports management, and sports broadcasting. As sports develop, many related professions are also advancing. This has opened new avenues of employment and entrepreneurship for young people.
Friends,
Whatever field we may be in today, we must work hard for our own success. At the same time, we must also take responsibility for shaping the next generation. Now you possess the experience of international tournaments. Therefore, I would request that you devote some time to those children who dream of progressing just as you did. You must water their dreams with the sweat of your own efforts. That is how success comes. Whenever you get an opportunity, meet children in your village and your town. Visit different schools. Be sure to visit the grounds where you first began playing. Your experiences can be extremely valuable to those children. Perhaps a single word from you may give a child the courage to move forward in sports.
Friends,
The youth of the country do not draw inspiration from you only in sports. Because the role of sports extends beyond the playing field. Sports teach us discipline in life. They teach us how to rise again after falling. They teach us how to win after losing. Sports teach us how to stay committed to a goal for a long time and how to adapt ourselves to changing circumstances. These lessons become part of our everyday lives. And this sporting spirit serves us throughout our lives.
Friends,
I always say: The one who plays, blossoms. So keep playing, keep blossoming. Once again, my many best wishes to all of you for the upcoming competitions and for all your future efforts. Your enthusiasm and your confidence are the greatest strengths of New India. With this confidence, we must take India to new heights.
So come, once again, with full energy, say with me:
Viksit Bharat, We will Do it!

title: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurates five development projects worth  ₹3,350 crore in Ladakh

Our special focus is on the new generation of Ladakh; the youth here should receive quality education, get the opportunity to learn new technologies, and they should not have to depend on other cities; therefore, a major Centre of Excellence is being built in Leh: PM

date:

content:
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated and dedicated five major development projects worth around ₹3,350 crore in Ladakh today via video conferencing. Celebrating a new chapter in the region's development through virtual participation, the Prime Minister inaugurated multiple key projects designed to ease travel, improve electricity and water access, and preserve ancient heritage. He fondly noted the enthusiasm of citizens waving the Tricolor amidst fresh snowfall in Zanskar, while extending his gratitude to the engineers, laborers, local workers, and the BRO personnel who executed these challenging works."I extend my heartiest congratulations to all the people of Ladakh for these projects,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Recalling his earlier laying of the foundation stone for the Kushok Bakula Rinpoche Airport terminal in Leh, the Prime Minister expressed delight at inaugurating the 650-crore-rupee facility that triples flight capacity and expands annual passenger handling from 10 lakh to 35 lakh. He highlighted that the terminal is India's first to feature geothermal heating alongside solar energy usage to suit the harsh climate, energizing local tourism while balancing infrastructure growth with ecological care."Our effort is to develop modern infrastructure in Ladakh while taking full care of the local environment,” asserted Shri Modi.
Underscoring the strategic and economic value of regional connectivity, the Prime Minister dedicated the 2,500-crore-rupee Nimmu–Padum–Darcha road to the citizens, noting that it slashes travel time from 12 hours down to just 3 hours. He emphasized that beyond saving commuters' time, this vital corridor will significantly boost local commerce."This road will also greatly help trade and business,” noted Shri Modi.
Building upon his prior inauguration of the Srinagar-Leh transmission line, the Prime Minister dedicated the Hanu hydroelectric project and its associated transmission network while noting ongoing modern power generation initiatives in Puga Valley. He explained that reliable electricity transforms rural life by illuminating homes and empowering children's education, healthcare delivery, and small-scale enterprises."Every sector will benefit from it,” observed Shri Modi.
Focusing on agricultural resilience and water security across the high-altitude terrain, the Prime Minister dedicated 40 newly constructed reservoirs developed under Project Amrit Him Sarovar to the local community. He stated that these water bodies are designed to support the agrarian economy during critical cultivation cycles."These will help in providing water for irrigation to farmers at the time of need,” noted Shri Modi.
The Prime Minister detailed sweeping infrastructural gains since Ladakh became a Union Territory in 2019. He noted that the road network has expanded from 1,800 kilometers to over 4,000 kilometers, major bridges have increased from 19 to nearly 75, helipads have grown from 7 to over 40, tap water coverage has surged from 3.5 percent to nearly 99 percent of households, hospital beds have doubled, and the ongoing Zojila Tunnel is set to provide all-weather national connectivity."Today, for the Central Government, the development of Ladakh is a top priority,” asserted Shri Modi.
Highlighting targeted efforts to unlock new avenues of regional prosperity, the Prime Minister pointed to the active promotion of winter and adventure tourism across the territory. He added that over 40 border settlements are currently being upgraded under the Vibrant Villages program to stimulate grassroots economic activity."This is creating employment opportunities even in far-flung villages,” noted Shri Modi.
Illustrating the rapid expansion of hospitality and modern agriculture, the Prime Minister observed that local homestays have multiplied from roughly 150 to 3,000. He simultaneously highlighted the continuous promotion of protected cultivation, which has resulted in 11,000 operational greenhouses across the region."These have created new possibilities for increasing farmers' income,” observed Shri Modi.
Addressing a long-standing regional demand for closer judicial access, the Prime Minister announced that the government officially approved the establishment of a High Court Bench for Ladakh in August this year. He stated that fulfilling this crucial institutional requirement will streamline both governance and legal recourse for citizens."This will make the justice system accessible alongside administration,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Emphasizing the role of digital connectivity in driving modern commerce for hotels, restaurants, homestays, and local crafts, the Prime Minister detailed the expansion of BharatNet and high-speed internet across remote pockets of the territory. He explained that continuous efforts are underway to ensure seamless access to e-governance, online education for youth, and global market integration for local entrepreneurs."Today online business is opening new avenues of income,” noted Shri Modi.
Prioritizing the educational empowerment of the younger generation so they do not have to migrate to other cities, the Prime Minister highlighted the construction of a major Center of Excellence in Leh alongside advancing proposals for satellite campuses of IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu. He stated that these premier institutions will equip local students with advanced research and modern technological skills right at their doorstep."The youth of Ladakh will be able to get better opportunities for higher education, research, and new skills right in their own region,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Recognizing the distinct athletic identity carved out by local youth in ice hockey, winter sports, and mountaineering, the Prime Minister welcomed the implementation of Ladakh's new sports policy to nurture regional talent. He reiterated the administration's commitment to providing world-class training facilities to help local athletes excel globally."We are striving to provide the local youth with enhanced training and facilities so they can scale new heights on national and international platforms,” asserted Shri Modi.
Praising the exceptional craftsmanship of local artisans and farmers, the Prime Minister shared how he frequently gifts Ladakhi products, having presented them to the German Chancellor, the Swedish Prime Minister, and the President of Kyrgyzstan, while highlighting the vast commercial potential of sea-buckthorn, handicrafts, GI-tagged apricots, high-altitude commercial floriculture, and the traditional Pashmina crafted by the Changpa community. He stressed that the government is actively strengthening Pashmina's global identity and expanding market branding for regional goods."Our effort is that the products here get new markets, get better branding, and their benefits reach the producers directly!” asserted Shri Modi.
Honoring the priceless cultural heritage of ancient monasteries, Buddhist traditions, and festivals inspired by Revered Kushok Bakula Rinpoche, the Prime Minister inaugurated India's first Petroglyph Conservation Park in Leh to safeguard historic rock art. He emphasized that preserving this legacy ensures both future generations and global visitors can deeply connect with the region's antiquity."People coming from the country and the world will also become familiar with the rich history of Ladakh,” affirmed Shri Modi.
Concluding his address with deep optimism for the territory's trajectory, the Prime Minister reiterated his faith in collective action to elevate the region to unprecedented developmental milestones. He offered his final congratulations and traditional greetings to the citizens for the newly launched infrastructure works."Together we all will take Ladakh to new heights of development,” affirmed Shri Modi.

title: English rendering of PM's speech at the launch of development projects in Ladakh via Video Conferencing
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 2:41PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lieutenant Governor Shri V. K. Saxena ji, all senior officials of the BRO and the Airport Authority, all officials of the Union Territory, other distinguished guests, my dear brothers and sisters.
“Ladakh si Mi-Mangs Kunla, Jullay!”
Today, another chapter is being added to the progress and development of Ladakh. I am happy that I am becoming a part of this occasion through technology. Today, several important development projects have been inaugurated in Ladakh. Through these projects, travel will become easier for many people, electricity facilities will improve in some places, water availability will increase in others, and the conservation of our ancient heritage will also receive new strength. Just now, I was watching that there was snowfall in Zanskar, and I was seeing the enthusiasm of the people of Zanskar, their excitement in waving the Tricolour even while the snow was falling.
Friends,
This is my Leh, my Ladakh. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all the people of Ladakh for these projects. I also congratulate all the engineers, workers, and local companions involved in these projects. I especially appreciate the companions of the BRO.
Friends,
Some time ago, I had the privilege of laying the foundation stone for the terminal building of the Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh. And it is my good fortune that today I have also had the privilege of inaugurating this important project. This terminal, built at a cost of about six hundred and fifty crore rupees, will increase the airport’s annual passenger capacity from one million to three and a half million. The number of flights here can also increase by up to three times. This terminal has another special feature. Keeping Ladakh’s harsh climatic conditions in mind, geothermal technology has been used in it. Solar energy has also been incorporated. This is the country's first airport terminal equipped with geothermal heating facilities in India. Congratulations to all of you. Our effort is that modern infrastructure should develop in Ladakh while also ensuring complete care for the environment here. This airport terminal will also provide new energy to the tourism sector in Ladakh. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to all my brothers and sisters of Ladakh for this modern airport terminal.
Friends,
The other projects inaugurated today are also of great importance. Today, the Nimmu–Padum–Darcha road has been dedicated to the people of Ladakh. About two thousand five hundred crore rupees have been spent on it. A journey that earlier took around twelve hours can now be completed in approximately three hours. This means that not only will travel time be saved, but this road will also greatly support trade and commerce.
Friends,
Earlier, I had the privilege of laying the foundation stone and inaugurating the power transmission line connecting Srinagar and Leh. Today, the Hanu hydroelectric project and its associated transmission line have also been inaugurated. We all know that a reliable electricity system brings not only light, but also illuminates lives. It brings major changes to life. Many new activities become possible in villages. Children’s education, healthcare services, and small local businesses, every sector will benefit from it. Work is also progressing on a modern electricity generation project in the Puga Valley.
Friends,
Today, forty reservoirs built under Project Amrit Him Sarovar have also been dedicated to the people of Ladakh. These will help farmers obtain irrigation water whenever needed.
Friends,
It has always been said that life in Ladakh is very difficult because of nature. Natural conditions do present their own challenges. But unfortunately, despite these circumstances, previous governments did not give priority to the development of Ladakh. Today, however, the development of Ladakh is a major priority for the central government. Since becoming a Union Territory, even greater attention has been given to its development needs. Until 2019, Ladakh had about 1,800 kilometres of road network. Today, it has increased to more than 4,000 kilometres. Earlier, there were nineteen major bridges here. Today, their number has increased to about seventy-five. The number of helipads has also increased from seven to more than forty. Earlier, only about three and a half percent of houses in Ladakh had access to tap water. Today, nearly 99 percent of homes have access to tap water. The number of beds in Ladakh’s hospitals has also doubled. Along with this, work on important projects such as the Zojila Tunnel is progressing very rapidly. Once completed, it will provide Ladakh with improved year-round connectivity to the rest of the country.
Friends,
The central government is also focusing on creating new avenues of prosperity in Ladakh. Today, opportunities in tourism are increasing here. Winter tourism and adventure tourism are being promoted. Under the Vibrant Villages Programme, the central government and we are developing more than forty border villages in Ladakh, and we call them the “first villages” of India. This is creating employment opportunities even in remote areas.
Friends,
Earlier, Ladakh had around one hundred and fifty homestays. Today, their number has increased to three thousand. Greenhouse farming has also been consistently promoted in Ladakh. Today, there are eleven thousand greenhouses here. These have created new possibilities for increasing farmers’ incomes.
Friends,
The demand for a High Court Bench in Ladakh had also existed for a long time. Our government has fulfilled that demand as well. In August this year, approval was granted for the establishment of a High Court Bench in Ladakh. This will make both administration and the justice system more accessible.
Friends,
Today, digital technology is also bringing many new opportunities closer. Whether it is hotels, restaurants, homestays, or local products, online business is opening new avenues of income. That is why we have expanded BharatNet and high-speed internet in Ladakh and other remote areas. Continuous work is also being done to ensure easier access to government services, to enable youth to study online, and to connect local entrepreneurs to national and global markets.
Friends,
We are paying special attention to the new generation of Ladakh. The youth here should receive quality education, opportunities to learn new technologies, and should not have to depend on other cities. Therefore, a major Centre of Excellence is being established in Leh. Proposals are also being advanced for satellite campuses of IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu. These will create better opportunities for higher education, research, and advanced skills for the youth of Ladakh within their own region.
Friends,
Ladakh also has enormous potential in sports. The youth here have created a distinct identity in areas such as ice hockey, winter sports, and mountaineering. I am happy that efforts are being made to promote sporting talent through Ladakh’s new sports policy. Our effort is to ensure that young people here receive better training and facilities so that they can achieve new milestones at national and international levels.
Friends,
The products that all of you create in Ladakh through your hard work are truly excellent. You already know that whenever I meet foreign guests, I often present products made in Ladakh as gifts and also tell them about all of you. I have gifted products made in Ladakh to the Chancellor of Germany, the Prime Minister of Sweden, and the President of Kyrgyzstan. The pashmina of this region, sea buckthorn, local handicrafts, and fruits such as apricots all carry immense commercial potential. That is why we granted a GI tag to Ladakh’s apricots. Today, their demand is increasing across the world. Our effort is to ensure that these products find new markets, receive better branding, and that the benefits reach the producers directly. We are also paying special attention to the pastoralists of the Changpa community. Efforts are being made to further strengthen the identity of the pashmina associated with their hard work and traditional skills. Commercial cultivation of flowers in high-altitude regions is also being promoted in Ladakh.
Friends,
The cultural heritage of Ladakh is a priceless treasure of our nation. The ancient monasteries here, the Buddhist traditions, and the local festivals must be preserved and safeguarded for future generations. In this direction, the contribution of the revered Kushok Bakula Rimpochee ji is a great inspiration for all of us. Our government’s effort is that people across the world become familiar with the culture and traditions of Ladakh. Keeping this mission in mind, India’s first Petroglyph Conservation Park has been inaugurated in Leh today. This will further strengthen efforts to preserve Ladakh’s ancient heritage. Future generations will be able to understand this heritage, and visitors from around the world will also become acquainted with Ladakh’s rich history.
Friends,
I am confident that together we will take Ladakh to new heights of development. With this, I once again extend my heartfelt congratulations to all of you for these many development works.
Thank you very much. Jullay!

title: Vice-President inaugurates KAUMARACON-2026 and launches digital initiatives of the All India Institute of Ayurveda
subtitle:
“Research Must Establish the Scientific Basis of Traditional Healthcare Practices for Their Global Acceptance”: Vice-President

“Ayurveda Has Great Potential in Preventive Healthcare, Nutrition and Child Development”: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav

“AIIA Has Emerged as a Leader in Ayurvedic Education, Research and Clinical Care”: Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha

Digital Initiatives Launched at KAUMARACON-2026 to Advance Research, Innovation and Clinical Practice
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 5:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated KAUMARACON-2026 at the All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Ayush. The event is the third international conference on Kaumarabhritya (Ayurvedic paediatrics). It is being held from 15 to 17 October 2026 under the theme “Shaping the Future of Child Health: Global Perspectives, Research Innovations, and Clinical Frontiers in Kaumarabhritya.” The occasion also marked the Institute’s Foundation Day. It celebrated a decade of progress in Ayurvedic education, clinical services, scientific research and innovation.
The Vice-President called for greater scientific research to establish the efficacy of traditional healthcare practices, strengthen patient confidence and enhance the global acceptance of India’s traditional systems of medicine. He
noted that India’s traditional systems of medicine represent a valuable legacy rooted in its civilisational wisdom and centuries-old knowledge traditions.
He also highlighted the international recognition of Yoga and the establishment of the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in Jamnagar as important milestones in sharing India’s traditional knowledge with the world.
Referring to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of developing AIIA at par with AIIMS, the Vice President said the Institute was progressing towards realising this vision.
Congratulating AIIA on its 10th Foundation Day, he emphasised the importance of sustained efforts in research, innovation and academic excellence to further strengthen the Institute’s standing.
He called upon researchers and practitioners to preserve traditional wisdom, strengthen it through scientific validation and place child health at the centre of their efforts.
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health and Family Welfare, Shri Prataprao Jadhav, highlighted the transformative journey of India’s traditional systems of medicine over the past decade under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He also noted that Ayurveda and other traditional healthcare systems, once often regarded as alternative approaches, are increasingly being integrated into the broader healthcare framework through institutional development, scientific research, quality assurance and evidence-based clinical practices.
Referring to the Ministry of Ayush’s 11-year progress, Shri Prataprao Jadhav highlighted the growing public trust in Ayush systems, the expansion of healthcare services and India’s increasing international recognition in traditional medicine. The Minister commended AIIA for emerging as a leading institution in this transformation. He noted that since its dedication to the nation by the Prime Minister in 2017, the Institute has strengthened its academic and clinical capabilities, earned NAAC A++ accreditation, expanded its specialised outpatient services and advanced its research infrastructure.
Emphasising the significance of KAUMARACON-2026, Shri Jadhav said that child health must remain a national priority and that India’s classical Ayurvedic knowledge offers valuable perspectives on preventive healthcare, maternal and child nutrition, growth and development. He underscored the importance of combining this traditional knowledge with contemporary scientific methods to establish credible, safe and effective approaches to paediatric healthcare.
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, described the occasion as an opportunity to reflect on the achievements of the Ayush sector and the institutional transformation of traditional medicine in India. He highlighted the Government’s efforts to strengthen Ayush through the National Ayush Mission, expanded healthcare access, research initiatives, quality assurance and international collaboration. He referred to the establishment of the WHO Global Centre for Traditional Medicine in Jamnagar and the growing availability of scientific literature through the Ayush Research Portal and Traditional Medicine Global Library.
Highlighting AIIA’s contribution, Vaidya Kotecha noted that the Institute operates more than 45 specialised OPDs, offers postgraduate and doctoral education across 12 specialties, mentors 105 pharmacovigilance centres and maintains more than 97 national and international academic collaborations. He also referred to the establishment of the AIIA satellite campus in Goa and the announcement of three new AIIA institutions in the Union Budget 2026–27.
Referring to the central role of Kaumarabhritya, the Secretary emphasised the importance of research, collaboration and innovation in strengthening paediatric healthcare. He expressed confidence that KAUMARACON-2026 would further advance Ayurveda’s contribution to child health and reinforce its role in India’s healthcare system.
Welcoming the dignitaries, Prof. (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, Director, AIIA, New Delhi described KAUMARACON-2026 as a significant milestone in the Institute’s journey towards completing a decade of service, academic advancement and scientific achievement. He expressed gratitude to the Vice-President for gracing the occasion and reaffirmed AIIA’s commitment to integrating classical Ayurvedic knowledge with contemporary scientific inquiry. He highlighted the Institute’s progress since its dedication to the nation in 2017, noting that AIIA has earned NAAC A++ accreditation and NABH quality recognition and has continued to expand its specialised clinical services, research facilities and academic programmes.
Prof. Prajapati emphasised that child healthcare is fundamental to building a healthy society. He highlighted the establishment of the KINDER Lab, which provides specialised facilities for paediatric electrophysiology and non-invasive diagnostics, and the Ayurinformatics Lab, which supports AI-driven formulation development and dosage design. He noted that the conference provides a valuable platform for sharing clinical insights, discussing translational research and exploring child-friendly therapeutic approaches. He expressed confidence that the scientific deliberations would foster international collaboration and open new avenues for improving child healthcare through research and innovation.
During the inaugural ceremony, the Vice-President inaugurated the Ayush Start-up Portal, the AIIA–iCAINE website and the Ayurveda Digital Innovation and Venture Acceleration Facility (AyuDIVA). He also launched the Vamana App and the Panchakarma Assessment App, marking an important step towards strengthening digital infrastructure, entrepreneurship and technology-enabled clinical practice in Ayurveda.
An international Memorandum of Understanding between Maharishi International University (MIU), USA, and AIIA, New Delhi, was also exchanged in the presence of the Vice-President, reflecting the Institute’s commitment to international academic and research collaboration.
Dr. Maneesha Upendra Kothekar, Chairperson, National Commission for Indian System of Medicine (NCISM), graced the occasion along with senior officials of the Ministry of Ayush and heads of various Ayush institutes. The conference also brought together eminent Vaidyas, paediatric healthcare specialists, researchers, academicians and international delegates from across the globe.
KAUMARACON-2026 will continue to deliberate on advances in Ayurvedic paediatric care, with scientific sessions and discussions aimed at strengthening evidence-based approaches to child health.

title: Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 celebrated today
subtitle:
Event highlights the pivotal role of women farmers  in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat

Union Agriculture Secretary Shri Atish Chandra  highlights  invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors; emphasises  the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 5:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India, celebrated Mahila Kisan Diwas 2026 today (15 October 2026 ) at the Dr. B. R. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, under the chairmanship of Shri Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare. The programme was organised to recognise the invaluable contribution of women farmers to Indian agriculture and highlight their pivotal role in advancing agricultural development and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat.
Sh. Atish Chandra, Secretary, Department of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (DA&FW), in his address, highlighted the invaluable contributions of women to agriculture and allied sectors, particularly in ensuring food security, sustaining rural livelihoods, managing natural resources and driving agricultural development. He emphasised the Government’s commitment to empowering women in agriculture through various initiatives, including direct income support, affordable institutional credit, technology transfer, skill development, farm mechanisation and improved access to agricultural marketing infrastructure.
महिला किसान दिवस के अवसर पर अपनी सभी किसान बहनों को प्रणाम करता हूं।

भारत गांव के बिना अधूरा है और गांव खेती के बिना और खेती महिलाओं के बिना नहीं हो सकती। अनादि काल से हमारी बहनें खेती में सबसे महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका का निर्वहन करती आ रही हैं। महिला किसान हमारी कृषि व्यवस्था की रीढ़ हैं और देश की खाद्य सुरक्षा एवं ग्रामीण अर्थव्यवस्था को मजबूती प्रदान कर रही हैं।

बदलते युग और खेती के तरीकों में आज बहनों की भूमिका खेती में बहुत महत्वपूर्ण हो गई है। अब ड्रोन दीदी है जो दवाओं का छिड़काव करती हैं, कृषि सखी हैं जो किसानों को कृषि पद्धतियों की ट्रेनिंग देती हैं, बैंक सखी हैं जो बैंक से टाई-अप करती हैं, पशु सखी हैं जो पशुपालन और दूध उत्पादन के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है।

title: Dr M L Jat addresses the Curtain Raiser press conference for ESTIC 2026 ;Dr Jat Outlines ICAR’s Role in ESTIC 2026
subtitle: Plenary talks, technical and parallel sessions, international collaboration forums, exhibitions and startup will be showcases in ESTIC 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 5:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) highlighted its research priorities, technological innovations and contributions to sustainable agriculture during a curtain-raiser and media interaction for the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026 at ICAR–Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal, Haryana, today. Dr. M. L. Jat, Secretary, Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE) and Director General, ICAR, outlined the Council’s role in the thematic area of “Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition” at the national conclave, scheduled to be held from 27th to 29th October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
ESTIC 2026 will bring together science-related ministries and departments, research institutions, startups and other stakeholders to showcase advances across 12 thematic areas. The thematic exhibition will feature 13 departmental stalls, 50 deep-tech startups and 10 departmental technologies. The conclave will provide a platform for presenting research outcomes, fostering scientific collaboration and connecting discoveries with practical applications.’
Highlighting ICAR’s research priorities, Dr. Jat emphasised a whole-of-government approach and coordination across various ministries. He outlined key areas including genome editing, bio-fortified crop varieties, climate-resilient agriculture, integrated pest management, horticultural diversification, livestock health, fisheries, natural resource management and agricultural mechanisation. He noted that scientific innovations must move beyond research laboratories and reach farmers through effective seed systems, technology dissemination and field-level adoption.
Among the featured scientific achievements are the world’s first two genome-edited rice varieties and India’s first telomere-to-telomere (T2T) reference genome of pigeonpea. These advances in crop genetics and precision breeding can support further research into improved crop traits and agricultural productivity.
Animal health and food security will be another focus, with the exhibition highlighting indigenous vaccine research, including an African swine fever (ASF) vaccine. The presentation describes a cell-adapted Indian ASF virus developed using MA-104 cells and reports protective effects in a target animal population. The precise technical description and protection claim should be confirmed against the official ICAR presentation before publication. ICAR’s wider animal-health research also includes vaccine development against lumpy skin disease, livestock genomics and the conservation of indigenous breeds.
The exhibition will also feature “Soil Intelligence: AI and Pedological Science,” highlighting the application of artificial intelligence and soil science to digital agriculture and soil-resource assessment. Such approaches can support data-driven soil management and inform planning for agricultural production and wider infrastructure development. ICAR’s research in this area emphasises the importance of understanding soil properties, improving resource-use efficiency and developing resilient farming systems.
On crop science and horticulture, Dr. Jat highlighted improved crop varieties, climate resilience, nutritional quality and advanced breeding technologies. He stated that ICAR had developed 117 horticultural crop varieties during the previous year. Research on biofortified crops and diversified farming systems is also aimed at supporting better nutrition and sustainable agricultural production.
In natural resource management, ICAR is working on soil health, water management, climate resilience and sustainable farming practices. Research on green ammonia explores the use of hydrogen produced with solar energy to manufacture ammonia as a potential alternative pathway for fertiliser production. Demonstrations covering 10,000 acres across six states were highlighted during the interaction, with collaboration involving ICAR, the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy and other stakeholders.
ICAR’s research portfolio also includes fisheries and aquaculture, livestock health, integrated pest management and agricultural mechanisation. Work on shrimp farming in saline areas seeks to expand productive use of underutilised land and water resources, while agricultural engineering initiatives, including cotton-harvesting machinery, aim to improve farm-operation efficiency and address labour constraints.
The SEHAT initiative—Science Excellence for Health through Agricultural Transformation, developed jointly by ICAR and the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) was also highloghted. The initiative connects agriculture, food and human health through approaches including biofortified crops and integrated farming systems. ICAR–National Dairy Research Institute (NDRI) has also developed a rapid on-site milk adulteration detection kit for identifying potential adulteration.
The technical session on “Agri-Tech, Food Systems and Nutrition” will bring together experts for discussions on agricultural innovation, food systems and nutritional security. The programme lists Dr Dr Ismahane Elouafi as keynote speaker, Dr. Ashwani Pareek and Prof. Peeyush Soni among the session speakers. The panel discussion will feature Dr. T. R. Sharma, Ms. Niima, Dr. Rabi N. Sahu, Dr. Firoz Hossain, Dr. Bhagirath Chaudhary and Dr. Kutubuddin Molla.
Earlier, welcoming the participants, the Director of ICAR-CSSRI highlighted the institute’s work on the characterisation and reclamation of salt-affected soils, management of poor-quality water and development of salt-tolerant varieties. The curtain-raiser and media interaction sought to build awareness of ESTIC 2026 and demonstrate the role of agricultural science and technology in advancing food and nutritional security, farmer prosperity and sustainable agricultural development.

title: Union Commerce and Industry Minister Shri Piyush Goyal Launches National Strategic Trade Command Centre at Vanijya Bhawan
subtitle:
NSTCC Aims to Strengthen Data-Driven Monitoring, Trade Intelligence and Evidence-Based Decision-Making

NSTCC to Enable Product-Wise and Market-Wise Trade Analysis, Identify Export Opportunities and Strengthen India's Global Trade Positioning
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry, Shri Piyush Goyal, launched the National Strategic Trade Command Centre (NSTCC) at Vanijya Bhawan, New Delhi, in the presence of Commerce Secretary, Shri Rajesh Agrawal, and Director General, Director General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Shri Lav Agarwal.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Piyush Goyal lauded NSTCC for enabling data-driven, evidence-based trade decisions. While reviewing the SCOMET (Special Chemicals, Organisms, Materials, Equipment and Technologies) dashboard, in particular, he called for regular meetings of the Inter-Ministerial Committee, weekly if required, to clear the backlog of pending applications and ensure that all applications are cleared expeditiously.
Developed by the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, NSTCC is a strategic initiative aimed at strengthening the monitoring, analysis and governance of India's international trade ecosystem through integrated data analytics and evidence-based decision-making.
The Command Centre has been conceptualised to provide senior policymakers and government officials with a consolidated view of India's trade performance, export promotion schemes, regulatory approvals, application processing and operational indicators. By bringing together information from multiple trade-related systems, NSTCC seeks to facilitate timely identification of emerging trends, operational bottlenecks and areas requiring policy or administrative intervention.
At the core of NSTCC is an integrated analytics and visualisation platform developed to transform trade-related data into actionable insights. NSTCC provides interactive dashboards covering key trade indicators, scheme performance, application pendency, processing timelines, regional trends and compliance-related parameters.
The platform enables users to analyse information across multiple levels, including national trade performance, Regional Authorities, schemes, products, destination markets and individual applications, subject to role-based access permissions.
In its initial phase, the Command Centre brings together dashboards covering key DGFT functions and trade-related domains, including Importer Exporter Code (IEC), Advance Authorisation, Export Promotion Capital Goods (EPCG), Certificate of Origin (CoO), SCOMET, restricted imports and exports, and other regulatory and trade facilitation processes. These dashboards will enable monitoring of scheme utilisation, processing efficiency, export obligations, trade patterns and operational performance across Regional Authorities.
The NSTCC is designed to support three key dimensions of trade governance:
• Integrated Monitoring: Providing consolidated visibility into trade trends, application processing, pendency and emerging risks, enabling timely identification and resolution of operational issues.
• Performance Assessment: Facilitating monitoring and benchmarking of schemes, processes and Regional Authorities against defined performance indicators to identify gaps and opportunities for improvement.
• Evidence-Based Policy Inputs: Identifying recurring bottlenecks, procedural complexities and emerging trade patterns to support policy simplification, process improvements and targeted trade facilitation measures.
The initiative also seeks to strengthen India's trade intelligence capabilities by enabling product-wise and market-wise analysis, assessment of trade agreement utilisation, identification of export opportunities and monitoring of India's trade positioning across international markets.
NSTCC has been designed to leverage existing digital infrastructure, including DGFT systems and the Trade Connect ePlatform, while providing a framework for progressive integration of additional datasets from other departments and trade-related agencies.
Going forward, the Command Centre is envisaged to evolve into a broader whole-of-government decision-support mechanism, with phased access for authorised stakeholders, including relevant ministries, states, Export Promotion Councils and other institutions. Its analytical capabilities will also be progressively strengthened through additional data integration, automated alerts and advanced analytics.
The launch of NSTCC marks an important step towards proactive, transparent and responsive trade governance, enabling the Department of Commerce and DGFT to move from periodic reporting towards continuous monitoring, coordinated intervention and evidence-based policy formulation.
The initiative reinforces the Government of India's commitment to leveraging digital technologies and data-driven governance to strengthen trade facilitation, improve administrative efficiency and enhance India's competitiveness in global trade.

subtitle:

India’s Youth Must Focus on Emerging Technologies, Cybersecurity and Lifelong Learning to Prepare for Future Job Opportunities: Shri Goyal
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 3:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal called upon young Indians to embrace emerging technologies, continuously upgrade their skills and contribute to India’s journey towards becoming a developed nation by 2047. Addressing the inauguration of the SRCC Centenary Conclave on
“
Pathways to Viksit Bharat”
,
he emphasised that investments in manufacturing, technology adoption and skill development would create opportunities for India’s youth and strengthen the country’s position in the global economy.
Shri Goyal said that countries are increasingly being assessed as manufacturing and investment destinations on the basis of political stability, resilient supply chains and fair and transparent trading practices. He noted that India has an opportunity to attract investments, expand manufacturing and adopt new technologies, including in northern and northeastern India, to generate employment and support economic growth.
He called upon young people to prepare for the changing employment landscape by developing skills in AI, cybersecurity and the practical application of emerging technologies. Shri Goyal said that large language models and other AI systems would need to be developed into practical tools that businesses and ordinary citizens could use. Drawing a parallel with India’s growth in the information technology sector during the 1990s and 2000s, he urged the youth to take a leading role in developing and applying new technologies rather than limiting themselves to their adoption.
Shri Goyal also emphasised the importance of continuous learning and personal development. He encouraged students to view skill enhancement as a lifelong responsibility and to identify emerging opportunities that could help them contribute to business growth, ease of doing business and ease of living. title: Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat Inaugurates ‘TAKSHANAM’, An Exhibition Bringing Together 150 Artists and Over 250 Sculptures at NGMA
subtitle: Exhibition celebrates India’s rich sculptural heritage and contemporary practices; introduces the sale of artworks at NGMA for the first time to support artists
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 9:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Culture and Tourism Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat inaugurated TAKSHANAM, a major exhibition featuring over 250 sculptures by 150 participating artists representing diverse generations, artistic backgrounds and approaches to sculptural expression, at the National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), New Delhi. Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, was also present on the occasion. Conceived as a shared platform for artistic encounter and exchange, the exhibition explores the continuities, transitions and new possibilities shaping the evolving landscape of Indian sculpture.
Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Union Minister of Culture and Tourism, said, “Art is an important expression of India’s cultural identity and creative spirit. Initiatives such as
TAKSHANAM
bring artists and audiences closer while encouraging greater appreciation of our artistic traditions and contemporary expressions. By creating space for both established and emerging talent, the exhibition reinforces the importance of nurturing creativity and expanding public engagement with art.”
Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture, said, “The Ministry of Culture remains committed to encouraging artistic excellence and creating meaningful opportunities for artists across the country.
TAKSHANAM
brings together diverse artistic voices and provides a platform for their work to reach wider audiences. The initiative to offer artworks for sale is also a noteworthy step towards strengthening engagement between artists, collectors and art enthusiasts.”
Speaking about the exhibition, Dr. Sanjeev Kishor Goutam, Director General, National Gallery of Modern Art, highlighted India’s longstanding sculptural tradition and the need to recognise and support contemporary practitioners. He said, “India has an extraordinary sculptural heritage that reflects its history, cultural achievements and artistic vision. From the Harappan and Mohenjo-daro civilisations, with their terracotta and metal objects and iconic works such as the Dancing Girl and the
Priest-King
sculpture, to the magnificent sculptural traditions associated with temple architecture and sites such as Ajanta, Ellora and Khajuraho, sculpture has played a significant role in expressing India’s cultural identity. This legacy continues in contemporary practice, with Indian artists such as Anish Kapoor and Subodh Gupta achieving international recognition for their work.
Inspired by the Sanskrit root
takṣ
(तक्ष्), meaning to carve, shape and fashion,
TAKSHANAM
reflects on sculpture as an evolving process shaped by the interplay of thought, experience, material and form. Bringing together works by artists across generations and artistic practices, the exhibition highlights the dynamic relationship between India’s rich sculptural heritage and contemporary innovation.
The exhibition features two distinct sections. The first, Eminent Artists, showcases works by experienced and veteran artists whose practices have contributed to the development of Indian sculpture. The second, Open Call Artists, presents works by approximately 80–90 artists selected by a jury following an open call. The exhibition also includes artworks from NGMA’s collection, creating opportunities for dialogue between established practitioners and artists exploring new creative possibilities.
A significant highlight of
TAKSHANAM
is the first-time initiative to offer artworks for sale at NGMA. The initiative aims to create opportunities for artists to reach collectors and art enthusiasts while encouraging wider engagement with sculptural art. By facilitating greater visibility and potential avenues of financial support, NGMA seeks to contribute to the sustainability of artistic practice, particularly in a medium that often involves substantial material costs, specialised skills and long production timelines.
Through
TAKSHANAM
, NGMA seeks to celebrate the depth of India’s sculptural heritage while recognising the contribution of contemporary practitioners to its continuing evolution. By bringing together veteran artists, jury-selected participants and works from its collection, the exhibition creates a space for artistic exchange, public engagement and greater appreciation of sculpture as an important medium of cultural expression.
The exhibition will remain open to visitors until
15 November 2026
at the National Gallery of Modern Art, Jaipur House, India Gate, New Delhi.
About the National Gallery of Modern Art
The National Gallery of Modern Art (NGMA), under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India, is a premier institution dedicated to the preservation, promotion and appreciation of modern and contemporary Indian art. Through exhibitions, educational initiatives and public engagement programmes, NGMA works to foster a deeper understanding of India’s artistic heritage and its evolving creative expressions.
