subtitle:
“Any terror act originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response”

“India is committed to peace, but it should not be mistaken for weakness; We’re fully prepared to safeguard sovereignty, integrity & national interests”

“Raksha Mantri Warns of Emerging Threat of ‘White-Collar Terrorism’ and Lone-Wolf Attacks, Calls for Heightened Vigilance

Heightened vigilance and responsible action by citizens key to tackling emerging threat of White-Collar Terrorism’ & Lone-Wolf Attacks, says RM

Shri Rajnath Singh calls for ‘Smart Power’ approach, combining advanced weaponry, AI and cost-effective defence technologies
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 1:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
“Operation Sindoor, Balakot Airstrikes and Surgical Strikes weren’t just military operations; they symbolised a decisive shift in the nation’s approach, moving from diplomatic condemnation to proactive action aimed at rooting out terrorism by reaching its very source,” said Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh at a Defence Conclave in New Delhi on October 15, 2026. Reiterating India’s stand on cross-border terrorism, he asserted that any further terrorist acts originating from Pakistan would invite an even stronger response. He emphasised that while India’s cultural ethos favoured dialogue, coexistence and peaceful resolution of disputes, its commitment to peace should not be mistaken for weakness. He added that since 2014, the ‘shelf life’ of most terrorists had fallen to less than a year, with security forces neutralising them within a year of their taking up arms against India.
Raksha Mantri termed strength and capability as essential to maintaining peace, and underlined that India hopes for peace, but remains prepared for war that sometimes becomes necessary to protect the nation. “Our commitment to peace remains steadfast, yet we are fully prepared to confront any challenge. Our goal is to build an India that, while advocating for peace, remains vigilant when it comes to security and is fully capable of safeguarding its sovereignty, integrity, and national interests,” he said.
On the evolving security landscape, Shri Rajnath Singh underscored the need for heightened vigilance and preparedness in an era of hybrid, high-tech and hyper warfare. He highlighted the growing complexity of security threats in the digital age, identifying what he described as the ‘5D Security Threat’ - Disinformation, Destabilisation, Disruption, Deception and Destruction. He pointed out that terrorism was evolving beyond organised groups, and emerging threats include ‘lone-wolf’ attacks and ‘white-collar terrorism’, which make it increasingly difficult for security agencies to identify radicalised individuals and prevent potential attacks.
Raksha Mantri referred to the recent incident involving a co-pilot who allegedly attempted to crash a passenger aircraft and Captain Smit Machhar who risked his life to avert a major terror attack. “The incident underscored the threat posed by lone-wolf attackers while demonstrating how the courage and commitment of an individual could thwart the designs of those driven by hatred. A single alert and courageous individual could help foil an entire terrorist plot. The fight against terrorism requires not only the capabilities of security agencies but also the active participation of aware and responsible citizens,” he said.
On defence preparedness, Shri Rajnath Singh underscored the need to combine ‘hard power’ with ‘soft power’ and called for a shift towards ‘smart power’. “Modern defence strategies must integrate precision-guided weapons and loitering munitions with cost-effective weaponry, human intelligence with artificial intelligence, and advanced systems with low-cost, agile and adaptable technologies to address evolving security challenges,” he said.
Raksha Mantri attributed India’s growing confidence in its defence capabilities to reforms, changes in operational methods and a transformed mindset under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He stated that in the last twelve-and-a-half years, the Government has shifted its focus from meeting immediate defence requirements to building an Aatmanirbhar and future-ready defence ecosystem. He highlighted that reforms in licensing regulations and measures to improve ease of doing business helped expand the country’s defence manufacturing base, with more than 500 companies now engaged in the sector and hundreds of new industrial licences issued.
On the reforms in defence procurement, Shri Rajnath Singh said priority is being given to domestic industries for the modernisation of the defence forces through measures such as Defence Acquisition Procedure and ‘Buy Indian-Indigenously Designed, Developed and Manufactured’ category. He noted that 75 per cent of the modernisation budget has been earmarked for procurement from Indian industries, adding that the reforms had strengthened collaboration between the public and private sectors. The nation is shifting from a ‘Whole of Government Approach’ to a ‘Whole of Country Approach’ and, gradually to a ‘Whole of the People Approach’, with start-ups, MSMEs, individual innovators and large corporations contributing to national defence under the spirit of ‘Nation First’, he said.
Raksha Mantri described Operation Sindoor as a demonstration of India’s growing technological capabilities and the defence forces’ confidence in advanced indigenous systems, including the Akash missile system and BrahMos, alongside other cutting-edge equipment. He said the success of the operation reflected the growing confidence in India’s domestic defence industry and its contribution to national security. “The defence forces had issued five positive indigenisation lists covering 509 items, including defence equipment, weapon systems and platforms, with a sixth list prepared for release soon. Similarly, Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs) had identified 5,012 items for indigenisation, including Line Replacement Units, sub-systems, spares and components, of which 3,255 had been indigenised,” he said,
On the growth witnessed by the defence sector due to the Government’s efforts, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that defence production has risen to a record over Rs 1.78 lakh crore from Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, with defence exports touching an all-time high of Rs 39,000 crore from Rs 686 crore in 2013-14, and India defence products reaching nearly 100 countries. He exuded confidence that the nation would achieve defence production targets of Rs 2 lakh crore this year and Rs 3 lakh crore by 2029, and export defence equipment worth Rs 50,000 crore by 2029.
Raksha Mantri attributed the growth to reforms that simplified export procedures, including the introduction of the Defence EXIM Portal, online approvals, the Open General Export License, streamlined quality certification and the ‘Green Channel’ policy. These measures, he said, enhanced India’s global credibility and prepared domestic industries to compete in international markets.
Emphasising the importance of research, development and innovation in achieving Aatmanirbharta in defence, Shri Rajnath Singh highlighted that the government has created opportunities for start-ups, MSMEs and young innovators through initiatives such as iDEX, iDEX Prime and ADITI scheme. “The Ministry of Defence has approved procurement of goods and services worth over Rs 2,400 crore from start-ups and MSMEs and sanctioned projects exceeding Rs 1,500 crore for new technology development. As of March 2026, iDEX had engaged 676 start-ups and innovators and facilitated the signing of 551 contracts. From a few dozen defence startups in 2018, the ecosystem had grown to more than 2,000, with young enterprises working across drones, artificial intelligence, quantum technology, cybersecurity, robotics and other advanced fields,” he added.
On the expansion of India’s defence industrial ecosystem, Raksha Mantri said defence production was no longer confined to the public sector, as DPSUs, private industries, more than 16,000 MSMEs, supply units and innovation centres are all contributing to the sector. “The corporatisation of OFB has helped transform them from loss-making entities into profitable enterprises. The growing network of public and private stakeholders is India’s new defence industrial family,” he said.
Further highlighting the reforms in defence procurement, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that that the sector was undergoing modernisation and indigenisation with greater transparency and accountability. Citing progress in ammunition manufacturing, he said 159 of the 175 ammunition variants used by the Defence Forces were now indigenously produced, representing more than 90 per cent self-reliance in ammunition variants. Referring to India’s exports of bulletproof jackets to over 100 countries, he noted that the country was the fourth in the world to establish a national standard for bulletproof jackets aligned with international norms. He also spoke about the implementation of the One Rank One Pension scheme and the creation of the Chief of Defence Staff post, terming them as significant measures undertaken to strengthen the defence framework.
Raksha Mantri concluded the address by expressing confidence that, when India completes 100 years of its independence, it will become ‘Viksit Bharat’ and provide leadership to the world across domains, including technology, the economy, and defence.

title: Digital India BHASHINI Division and Government of Manipur Sign MoU to Advance Multilingual AI and Language Technology at BHASHINI Rajyam Workshop

content:
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, in collaboration with the Department of Information Technology, Government of Manipur, organised the BHASHINI Rajyam Workshop, Manipur Chapter, in Imphal on 14 October 2026. The workshop explored opportunities to advance multilingual artificial intelligence, strengthen language technology and integrate Indian language solutions into government and citizen-facing digital services.
The programme was graced by Shri Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Manipur, and brought together government representatives and other stakeholders to discuss the role of language technology in making digital services more accessible and inclusive.
A key outcome of the workshop was the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between DIBD and the Government of Manipur, represented by Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, DIBD, and Shri Somorjit Salam, IAS, Secretary, Information Technology, Government of Manipur. The MoU aims to strengthen cooperation in language technology, improve language resources and explore solutions for multilingual digital services across the state.
Addressing the gathering, Shri Yumnam Khemchand Singh, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Manipur, highlighted the potential of artificial intelligence and language technology to promote India’s linguistic diversity and expand opportunities for the state’s communities. “Through artificial intelligence and language technology, we are promoting India’s diverse languages and exploring opportunities to bring more of Manipur’s languages into the digital space. Our linguistic diversity is a valuable strength as we move forward,” he said.
Shri Somorjit Salam, IAS, Secretary, Information Technology, Government of Manipur, emphasised that digital services must be accessible and meaningful to the people they are intended to serve. “Digital services are effective only when people can understand and use them confidently. Through BHASHINI, we can address language barriers with carefully tested solutions that respond to Manipur’s needs and deliver lasting public benefit,” he said.
The workshop provided an overview of BHASHINI’s Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and its multilingual AI ecosystem, highlighting the role of language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications in enabling digital services across languages. Discussions explored how these capabilities could be integrated into government platforms and citizen-facing applications to support more accessible service delivery.
A live demonstration of real-time English-to-Manipuri translation showcased the potential of language technology to bridge communication gaps. The session also highlighted the importance of building digital language resources and validating language models using relevant data, with inputs from language experts and local communities, to improve their usefulness in real-world settings.
Speaking on the need to build language technologies that reflect India’s diversity, Shri Amitabh Nag, CEO, DIBD, said: “AI must understand India in all its linguistic diversity. Through our partnership with Manipur, we aim to strengthen language technologies, expand practical applications and ensure that language is not a barrier to accessing digital services or pursuing opportunities,” he said.
The workshop highlighted the linguistic diversity of Manipur, including Manipuri, Tangkhul, Thadou, Paite, Hmar, Liangmai and other languages spoken across the state. The state’s linguistic knowledge, local expertise and community participation can contribute to developing language technologies that better reflect regional needs and communication practices.
Sessions explored applications of multilingual AI in governance and citizen services, including education, healthcare, legal services and grievance redressal. BHASHINI शिल्पी, an interactive platform for developers, students and innovators, provided an opportunity to learn, experiment, solve problems and build with Language AI. Going beyond a conventional technology session, it encouraged participants to explore real-world challenges, exchange ideas and discover possibilities for developing, scaling and innovating with BHASHINI’s language technologies, services and APIs. The interactive Q&A further enabled participants to discuss potential applications and seek clarity on implementation. The BHASHINI Mitra initiative was also highlighted as an avenue for state institutions and language communities to contribute language data and strengthen multilingual AI resources.
As a next step, DIBD and the Government of Manipur will identify priority use cases, assess language-data requirements and explore the integration of BHASHINI’s language technologies into relevant government platforms. The collaboration will also focus on strengthening language resources and working with language experts and local communities to develop and validate solutions that reflect the state’s linguistic diversity and public service needs.
The BHASHINI Rajyam initiative aims to strengthen collaboration between BHASHINI and state governments, helping translate language technology capabilities into practical solutions that improve access to digital services and enable wider participation in India’s digital ecosystem.
About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, is advancing India’s Language-First Digital Public Infrastructure to enable multilingual access to digital services. BHASHINI brings together language datasets, AI models, APIs and applications to support government departments, developers, researchers and other stakeholders in building multilingual AI solutions. It powers more than 800 government websites, has enabled over 9 billion cumulative AI inferences and processes more than 24 million AI inferences daily. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian languages for text, 23 Indian languages for voice and 35 international languages, advancing the adoption of language technology across India’s digital ecosystem.

content:
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) conducted a special inspection drive in Gurugram on 14.10.2026 to assess the presence of visible road dust and the effectiveness of road-cleaning and sweeping operations. It’s a part of continued efforts to strengthen implementation of dust mitigation measures and improve road cleanliness for effective abatement of air pollution across Delhi-NCR.
During the inspection, a total of 258 violations were observed relating to high visible road dust, accumulation of Construction & Demolition (C&D) waste. Further, damaged footpaths and potholes were identified across the inspected road stretches. Out of these, 174 violations were observed on roads under the jurisdiction of Municipal Corporation of Gurugram (MCG) and 84 violations on roads under the jurisdiction of Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority (GMDA).
The Commission had deployed 4 Flying Squads to inspect roads under the jurisdiction of the MCG and GMDA. The observations made during the inspection drive indicate the need for strict and effective implementation of prescribed road-cleaning, sweeping and dust mitigation measures by the concerned road-owning agencies. The Commission has emphasized that regular and effective road-cleaning and sweeping operations are critical for controlling road dust and preventing its re-suspension due to vehicular movement. Accumulation of road dust and C&D waste, along with damaged footpaths and potholes, contribute to increased dust generation and resuspension due to vehicular movement, thereby adversely impacting ambient air quality.
Further, MCG, GMDA and other concerned agencies have been directed to take necessary corrective measures to control road dust and address the gaps observed during the inspection on priority basis. The Commission has emphasized that road stretches under the jurisdiction of concerned agencies should be maintained in a clean and dust-free condition through regular sweeping, removal of accumulated dust and C&D waste and timely corrective action(s). The Commission has underlined that in case of non-compliance, strict action including prosecution as per law, may be taken.

title: Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participates in the 114th meeting of the Development Committee Plenary of the World Bank in Bangkok, Thailand, today
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 9:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated as the Governor of the World Bank in the 114th Meeting of the Development Committee Plenary in Bangkok, Thailand, today. The agenda for the meeting was “Private Capital Mobilisation and Jobs”.
The Union Finance Minister delivered the following speech as India’s intervention on the topic of “Private Capital Mobilisation and Jobs”:
“We welcome the continued focus on mobilising private capital and creating jobs. At a time of growing energy market stress, trade fragmentation, climate pressures, and rapid technological change, productive and better-paid jobs remain the most effective pathway to poverty reduction and shared prosperity.
I wish to make six brief points.
First, jobs require ecosystems, not isolated interventions.
Sustainable job creation requires high-quality and inclusive economic growth, which in turn needs macroeconomic stability, efficient infrastructure, simple and certain regulations, and broad-based access to finance and skills. Our experience shows that last-mile connectivity to energy and job markets, large-scale physical and digital public infrastructure, financial inclusion, and regulatory trust in market forces are critical for improved productivity and jobs at scale.
Second, the private sector must remain at the centre of the development agenda.
Most jobs will be and should be created by private enterprises MSMEs and startups will play a big role. Mobilising private investment is therefore essential. At the same time, success should be measured not by the volume of financing mobilised, but by outcomes: jobs created and rise in productivity.
We encourage stronger collaboration among IBRD, IFC, and MIGA, and faster operationalisation of the WBG Guarantee Platform. Developing economies are constrained by a shortage of risk capital. Guarantees and risk mitigation instruments are among the most effective tools to accelerate risk-capital formation and crowding in private capital.
Third, competitive financing must remain a core priority.
The World Bank must remain a development partner through competitive pricing, tapping tools like local currency financing, stronger guarantee products, and lower transaction costs. Affordable, predictable, and accessible financing must remain and at the core of the Middle-Income strategy.
Fourth, the Knowledge Bank must help address market failures.
The most effective interventions from the World Bank Group would be in addressing market failures in critical areas like urbanisation, tourism, agricultural exports and critical minerals. Developing countries stand to benefit greatly from the boost to state capacity that can come from AI: it deserves much greater attention in the Bank's operational and knowledge agenda.
Fifth, we reiterate our longstanding concerns regarding Worldwide Governance Indicators and similar composite assessments.
Given their far-reaching implications, there is a need for a comprehensive review and revision of existing methodologies to ensure that they are transparent, objective, evidence-based, and better aligned with current realities and the diverse development experiences of member countries. This will be essential for preserving the integrity of the Bank's knowledge products.
Finally, evolution must strengthen voice and development impact.
The ultimate measure of success is whether reforms help countries create jobs, raise productivity, reduce poverty, and improve living standards. We also reiterate the importance of strengthening the voice and representation of developing countries in the governance architecture of the Bank.
Our constituency stands ready to work with fellow shareholders, management, and development partners to advance these objectives.”

title: DRI seizes around 6.2 kg foreign-origin gold; busts sophisticated gold smuggling modus operandi through unaccompanied baggage; three arrested
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 6:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), as part of its sustained crackdown on organised gold smuggling, has uncovered a new and sophisticated
modus operandi
involving the unaccompanied baggage channel. The network relied on insiders, including warehouse personnel, and intermediaries to retrieve smuggled gold from cargo and pass it to the intended recipient.
Based on specific intelligence, officers of Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) intercepted an unaccompanied baggage consignment at Air Cargo Complex, Trivandrum . Detailed examination of the baggage resulted in the recovery and seizure of
6.28 kg
foreign origin gold valued at
Rs. 9.18 crore
, ingeniously concealed inside various hardware items.
The gold was concealed inside various hardware items, including a floor spring, metal locks, a grease gun and a door closer. The modus operandi involved, packing these hardware items along with other articles in a trolley secured with a number lock whose combination had been pre decided among the members of the syndicate. The trolley was shipped as unaccompanied baggage from Dubai to Trivandrum. Upon arrival, the warehouse staff member would open the trolley using the pre decided combination, retrieve the hardware items containing the concealed gold, and hand them over to the mediator, who would, in turn, deliver
the same to the receiver.
Simultaneous searches conducted in connection with the operation led to the apprehension of three persons allegedly involved in the smuggling syndicate: a warehouse staff member tasked with retrieving the hardware items containing the concealed gold, a Customs Broker acting as a mediator, and a receiver who had travelled to Trivandrum to take delivery of the gold. All the three were arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962.
DRI remains committed to expose novel sophisticated modus operandi and bust the smuggling networks through intelligence led operations.

Initiatives under this campaign are being organised across the country to mark 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi
’
s ‘Seva’ and ‘Samarpan’, first as the Chief Minister of a state and subsequently as the Prime Minister of India. Under the campaign, assistive prosthetic devices are being provided in Chhattisgarh to make life easier for tribal persons with disabilities who have suffered as a result of Naxal violence.
Shri Amit Shah said that the programme had been held in Jagdalpur from 5 to 7 October 2026, benefiting more than 3,600 persons with disabilities. More than 1,570 beneficiaries were from Bastar alone, a figure that reflects the extent of suffering in the region. He said that five decades of Naxalism had inflicted immense suffering on the poor tribal communities of Bastar. He said that using IEDs to inflict disabilities on innocent civilians in pursuit of political objectives was the gravest violation of human rights. Shri Shah said that the Modi government had been firmly committed to eliminating Naxalism from the entire country before 31 March 2026, and that Naxalism had now been eliminated. However, he emphasised that the end of Naxalism alone would not erase five decades of suffering. We must heal the wounds inflicted by this suffering, help victims stand on their feet again, and ensure they can live with dignity and respect.
Union Home Minister said that the Chhattisgarh government, district administration, State Social Welfare Department, Bhagwan Mahaveer Viklang Sahayata Samiti, Jaipur, Bharatiya Jain Sanghatana and several others were contributing to this noble endeavour. He said that the Modi government was committed to providing every person with a disability and every victim an opportunity for rehabilitation. The Government of India, he added, stood firmly alongside the Chhattisgarh government in supporting these efforts. Shri Amit Shah said that every trace of Naxalism must be eliminated and Bastar must once again become a vibrant and thriving region. Significant work had already been undertaken in this direction, he said, adding that traditional tribal leadership in the Bastar region had made a major contribution. By providing persons with disabilities with wheelchairs, tricycles, crutches, hearing aids, smart walking sticks, artificial limbs and other assistive devices, the government could help usher in a new era of hope and happiness in Bastar.
Shri Amit Shah said that the Chhattisgarh Government had undertaken several initiatives, including the Bastar Olympics, Bastar Pandum, Niyad Nellanar and the Chief Minister’s Samuhik Bus Yojana, to transform Bastar, which has suffered from violence, into a vibrant and joyful region once again. He said that Bastar, where the sounds of gunfire and bomb blasts once created an atmosphere of fear, is now witnessing thousands of young people participating in sports and keeping their traditions alive. He said that in a region where the sounds of gunfire and bomb blasts once prevailed and fear was widespread, thousands of young people were now participating in sports and keeping their traditions alive. He said that Bastar Pandum had been a major initiative to revive tribal art and culture. Under the Niyad Nellanar scheme, significant efforts had also been made to expand basic infrastructure and extend essential services to Bastar, which had remained deprived of such facilities under opposition governments for five decades.
Union Home Minister and Minister of Cooperation said that approximately 8,526 Naxalites have surrendered. Bank accounts have been opened for 7328 of them who did not previously have accounts. A total of 1620 people have received reward money, 7,882 have received incentives, 455 have been provided jobs, and 129 have been allotted land. In addition, under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, 4014 beneficiaries have received houses, and more than 2308 tribal people have undergone skill development training. He further stated that 6763 new ration cards have been issued, 2808 families have been provided free electricity, and work has begun on 372 new road projects. Construction is underway on 670 small bridges, 48,526 people have been issued Aadhaar cards, and 44 gram panchayats have been recognised under the ‘Ilwad Panchayat Awards’.
Shri Amit Shah said that more than 500 security camps have been established, of which over 200 will be converted into Shaheed Veer Gundadhur Seva Dera. Officials of the Government of India and the Chhattisgarh government will now work from the very camps where security personnel once sat to protect the people, laying the foundation for a developed Bastar. He said that these public service centres would help the government realise its vision of a developed Bastar.

title: India Must Move from Being a Global Content Market to a Creator of Globally Competitive Media and Entertainment Companies: Secretary, I&B, at CII Big Picture Summit 2026
subtitle: CII releases white paper giving roadmap to building a $100 billion Indian Media and Entertainment sector
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 4:16PM by PIB Mumbai
content:
Mumbai : 15 October 2026
Shri Chanchal Kumar, Secretary, Ministry of Information & Broadcasting, Government of India, today called upon the media and entertainment industry to move beyond scale and focus on original intellectual property (IP), sustainable business models and global market expansion, with the objective of positioning India as a leading source of creative content, technology, talent and globally competitive media companies.
Addressing the inaugural session of the two day CII Big Picture Summit 2026, themed “The New Economics of Media and Entertainment: Building India’s Future Global Media Companies”, Shri Chanchal Kumar said India has the opportunity to translate its rich storytelling traditions, cultural diversity and creative talent into lasting economic and cultural value.
He linked the summit theme to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s WAVES 2025 vision of “Create In India, Create For The World”, emphasising both innovation and trust. Highlighting the Government’s efforts to strengthen India’s creative ecosystem, Shri Chanchal Kumar referred to initiatives such as WAVES, WAVES Bazaar, the Indian Institute of Creative Technologies (IICT) and India Cine Hub. He also underscored the importance of a robust anti-piracy framework to protect creativity and intellectual property, emphasising the vision of “Create in India. Own in India. Scale from India. Take it to the world.”
The summit also witnessed the release of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) White Paper, The New Economics of Media & Entertainment, which outlines a roadmap for India’s media and entertainment sector to reach $100 billion by the early 2030s. The paper calls for faster reforms, stronger regional markets and measurable implementation to accelerate the sector’s growth.
Mr Gaurav Banerjee, Summit Chair and MD & CEO, Sony Pictures Networks India, called for a fundamental rethink of business models. “A large audience is, finally, just a starting point. It is not a business model.”He urged greater focus on audience value, measurable advertiser outcomes and sustainable investor returns.
Ms Gunjan Soni, Summit Co-Chair and Country MD, YouTube India, described creativity and culture as economic strengths supporting India’s “Viksit Bharat” ambition. She said digital technology and AI could help a young generation of creators turn imagination and local identity into world-class enterprises.
Mr Rajan Navani, Summit Co-Chair and MD & CEO, JetSynthesys, said democratised access to technology and AI was essential to keeping pace with global change. AI, he said, was rapidly narrowing the gap between human imagination and the ability to realise ideas.
Shri Chanchal Kumar also inaugurated the WAVES Global Investor and Investee Meet, bringing together more than 150 investors and investees. The initiative connected nearly 20 participants from WaveX and WAVES Bazaar, strengthening links between capital providers and emerging creative businesses.

title: DDWS Organised 13th District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad to Strengthen Community Ownership, Source Sustainability and Service Delivery under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
subtitle: Five Districts from Uttar Pradesh, Tripura, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Jharkhand Showcase Innovative Practices in Rural Drinking Water Governance
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Drinking Water & Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, organised the
13th edition of the District Collectors’ Peyjal Samvad
today through video conferencing, bringing together senior officials, District Collectors/ District Magistrates, and Mission Directors of State/UTs to deliberate on accelerating the implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) 2.0 and sharing of best practices.
The Samvad was chaired by Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS. Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, Additional Secretary & Mission Director, National Jal Jeevan Mission (NJJM), and Senior Officers from DDWS were also present during the Samvad.
In his opening remarks,
Shri Ashok K.K. Meena, Secretary, DDWS
, said that this platform has emerged as an important platform for peer learning, enabling district administrations to share innovative practices and address implementation challenges in rural drinking water service delivery. He emphasised the pivotal role of District Collectors in strengthening local water governance, ensuring effective operation and maintenance of rural water supply systems, and promoting community ownership of assets created under the Mission.
Secretary, DDWS calls for Greater Accountability and Data-Driven Governance. He directed districts to ensure
regular monthly meetings of District Water and Sanitation Missions (DWSMs)
and timely uploading of meeting minutes on the DWSM Portal. He stressed that strong institutional monitoring and documentation are essential for transparency, accountability and effective programme implementation.
Highlighting the findings from
Jal Seva Aankalan
, Shri Meena urged districts to regularly review functionality assessment reports and district improvement plans available on the dashboard. He noted that water quality and energy-related disruptions continue to affect service delivery in many areas and called upon States and districts to explore solarisation of rural water supply schemes for improving reliability and operational efficiency.
He also emphasised the effective utilisation of the
Decision Support System (DSS)
, which integrates groundwater, rainfall, hydrological and Jal Jeevan Mission data. He encouraged district administrations to use the platform for evidence-based planning, identification of water-stressed areas, source sustainability planning and prioritisation of interventions.
Referring to the integration of drinking water sustainability efforts with other national initiatives, he urged districts to leverage convergence opportunities under
VB-G RAM G
and other programmes to undertake groundwater recharge, source protection and water conservation measures in vulnerable areas.
Secretary also emphasised that following the formal handover of drinking water supply schemes through
Jal Arpan,
the districts to retain the certificates in their respective local languages through Jal Arpan Module.
Shri Kamal Kishore Soan, AS&MD, NJJM
, in his address underscored the importance of strengthening grassroots institutions for long-term sustainability of rural drinking water systems. He highlighted the need for systematic training and capacity building of Gram Panchayats, Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs), Panchayat Secretaries and
Sujalam Shakti Groups
to support operation and maintenance of drinking water infrastructure.
He emphasised that district administrations should encourage greater
utilisation of the DSS platform
, strengthen source sustainability planning in water-stressed areas and ensure convergence with ongoing rural development initiatives and VB-G RAM G to protect drinking water sources.
Shri Soan also encouraged districts to provide
exposure visits for higher-secondary and senior school students
to multi-village water supply schemes, water treatment facilities, laboratories and SCADA-enabled systems so that young citizens develop a deeper understanding of water infrastructure and water conservation.
Shri Y.K. Singh, Director (NJJM),
made a presentation on the Jal Arpan module, highlighting its importance in ensuring the formal commissioning and handover of rural drinking water supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and communities. He explained the key stages of Jal Arpan preparedness, the reporting and monitoring framework through the DTU/DWSSM dashboard, and the digital workflow for Jal Arpan and Har Ghar Jal certification on the Gram Panchayat dashboard, while providing guidance on the step-by-step process for reporting and certification through the online module.
Innovative Best Practices Shared by Districts Through Presentations
During the Peyjal Samvad, a total of five districts presented their progress and best field practices which will further help other State’s districts to develop better under JJM 2.0. Each presentation was delivered by the respective District Collector/ District Magistrate.
Kanpur Nagar, Uttar Pradesh – Sh. Mahender Singh Tanwar, District Magistrate & Collector
highlighted the district's efforts towards strengthening service delivery through regular review meetings, inter-departmental coordination and community participation. The district has undertaken extensive IEC activities involving schools, sports clubs and social media platforms to promote awareness on water conservation, water quality and responsible use of drinking water infrastructure. Community-based water quality surveillance is being strengthened through trained women volunteers using Field Test Kits, while regular laboratory testing and quality audits are helping ensure safe drinking water supply. The district further showcased the use of technology-driven monitoring mechanisms, including SCADA-based systems, digital grievance redressal platforms and the Jal Saarthi application for improved service monitoring. Efforts are also underway to develop GIS-based mapping of drinking water assets for better infrastructure management and planning.
West Tripura, Tripura - Dr. Vishal Kumar, District Magistrate & Collector’s
presentation focused on strengthening community ownership and sustainability of drinking water systems through active involvement of Gram Panchayats, Self-Help Groups and local communities. The district has made significant progress in user-charge collection and has undertaken extensive capacity-building programmes for Gram Panchayats on operation and maintenance, source sustainability and monitoring of water supply systems. SHGs are playing an important role in awareness generation, community mobilisation and social audit-related activities, thereby enhancing accountability and local participation. Given the challenges associated with water availability, the district is placing special emphasis on source sustainability through catchment protection, afforestation, rooftop rainwater harvesting, groundwater recharge and greywater management interventions. Scientific source mapping, preparation of Village Water Security Plans and convergence with other development programmes are helping strengthen long-term water security. The district also highlighted community-led efforts, including the involvement of Jal Sakhis and local institutions in promoting sustainable management of drinking water assets.
Thanjavur, Tamil Nadu - Tmt. R. Revathi, District Collector,
showcased innovative practices aimed at strengthening drinking water security and sustainability through scientific planning and technology-led interventions. The district has undertaken village-level water budgeting exercises to assess present and future water demand, identify groundwater stress and guide investments in recharge and conservation measures. Community participation has been central to this exercise, with Gram Panchayats, VWSCs and local stakeholders actively involved in planning and implementation. The district has also promoted groundwater recharge, rooftop rainwater harvesting, rejuvenation of water bodies and micro-irrigation measures to improve long-term water security. He further highlighted the adoption of advanced technologies for improving drinking water service delivery. These include IoT-enabled real-time monitoring systems, digital dashboards and smart flow-monitoring mechanisms for tracking water supply performance and reducing losses. Low-cost water disinfection systems have also been introduced to strengthen water quality management. The Secretary appreciated the district's work on water budgeting and encouraged the exploration of innovative approaches, including assessment of the feasibility of continuous rural water supply in suitable areas.
Baragada, Odisha – Sh. Aditya Goyal, District Magistrate & Collector
shared the district's structured approach towards implementation of rural water supply projects through a three-stage framework covering execution, commissioning and operation & maintenance. Strong inter-departmental coordination has helped resolve issues relating to land, power supply, forest clearances and right-of-way permissions, enabling timely progress of drinking water infrastructure projects. The district has also institutionalised monthly review mechanisms and community participation during the commissioning stage to identify and address issues such as leakages, unauthorised connections and restoration of affected infrastructure. Bargarh has further strengthened service delivery through proactive grievance redressal arrangements, regular field inspections and periodic water quality monitoring. The district highlighted notable success in ensuring reliable water supply through large multi-village schemes, including provision of round-the-clock piped water supply to IIM Sambalpur. The experience reflects the importance of effective project management, community engagement and sustained monitoring in achieving dependable drinking water services.
Palamu, Jharkhand – Sh. Dilip Pratap Singh Shekhawat, District Magistrate & Collector
highlighted its robust monitoring mechanisms, including regular review meetings, a dedicated district control room and grievance redressal systems for tracking the functionality of drinking water schemes. Capacity building of Village Water and Sanitation Committees (VWSCs) and community-level institutions is being undertaken to facilitate effective operation and maintenance of water supply infrastructure after handover. The district also showcased innovative approaches for source sustainability and community engagement. Convergence with MGNREGA and other programmes is being utilised for groundwater recharge and rainwater harvesting works, while IoT-enabled monitoring systems are supporting real-time supervision of water supply schemes. Community-based water quality surveillance is being carried out through the combined efforts of Jal Sahiyas, Anganwadi Workers and Health Sahiyas. The district also highlighted its Jalkar Bhugtan Abhiyan, aimed at strengthening user-charge collection and ensuring sustainable operation and maintenance of rural drinking water infrastructure through greater community ownership and transparent financial management.
These presentations showcased achievements, ongoing challenges, and best practices under JJM underlining the diversity of approaches adopted to accelerate progress under Har Ghar Jal.

Presentations will include initiatives relating to cybersecurity frameworks, digital banking, animal disease management, blood bag traceability, education, urban governance and the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC).
The conference will provide a platform for participating states, districts and government organisations to share experiences, exchange ideas and explore opportunities to replicate successful initiatives. It will contribute to strengthening collaborative efforts towards responsive, transparent, efficient and technology-enabled governance.
The conference will conclude with a valedictory session featuring addresses by the Chief Secretary, Government of Himachal Pradesh, and Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG.

Key Ministries/Departments hold dedicated one-day campaign drives across their attached, subordinate and field offices

ministry: Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions
date:

content:
The Special Campaign 6 launched by the Government, with Department of Administrative Reforms & Public Grievances as the nodal department, has gained significant momentum. Following the successful completion of the Preparatory Phase on 30 September 2026, the Implementation Phase commenced on 2 October 2026 and will continue till 31 October 2026. In the first two weeks of implementation, Ministries/Departments across the Government have shown remarkable enthusiasm, taking up innovative, citizen-centric and sustainable initiatives to advance the objectives of Swachhata and disposal of pending matters.
The third meeting with Nodal Officers of Special Campaign 6 for Swachhata and Disposal of Pending Matters was held under the chairpersonship of the Secretary, DARPG, Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, to review the progress of the Implementation Phase of the campaign.
The meeting was attended by 600+ officers virtually from over 240 locations, representing 84 Ministries/Departments, their PSUs and field offices. During the meeting, Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG, presented the progress of the ongoing Campaign and highlighted the innovative initiatives taken up by Ministries/Departments.
A new feature of this year's campaign is the dedicated one-day drive, under which key Ministries/Departments take up cleanliness and disposal activities on a single day across all their attached and subordinate offices and field establishments. The impact of the dedicated one-day activity is evident in the wider outreach of Special Campaign 6, with field offices across various Ministries/Departments actively participating in the campaign activities.
Innovative initiatives:
Ministries/Departments have gone beyond routine cleanliness and taken up several innovative and citizen-centric initiatives during the campaign. Some of these are:
Citizen-centric services:
The Department of Posts launched the DigiPost initiative, a unique phygital mail service under which traffic e-challans issued by Gujarat Police are digitally transmitted and physically delivered to citizens. The Department of Defence established the e-Chhawani Helpdesk for grievance redressal, while the Ministry of Railways organised Rail Jan Yuva Samvaad to engage youth, students and passengers on railway issues and public participation.
E-waste management:
The Ministry of Coal set up an e-waste kiosk at the MCL headquarters and conducted e-waste collection drives across its field offices. The Ministry of Mines put up an e-waste collection stall at the GPOA-3 building to encourage responsible disposal of discarded electronic and electrical items under the Reduce, Reuse and Recycle approach. Under the Ministry of Education, obsolete e-waste was segregated and collected for disposal at IIIT Allahabad, and the Department of School Education and Literacy organised an e-waste collection drive.
Waste to Wealth:
Discarded material is being turned into art and useful products. The Ministry of Culture created a peacock sculpture from discarded plastic spoons and paper, and Re-Bot, a robot sculpture crafted from discarded computer parts and household waste. The Ministry of Railways developed a Waste to Art Park at the Rail Museum, and the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises made a working charkha out of discarded e-waste.

content:
The Capacity Building Commission (CBC) will hold the third regional workshop of Sādhana Śhrinkhla 2026 at Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, on 23 and 24 October 2026. The two-day consultation will bring together States and Union Territories of the Northern Region to deliberate on how Government Training Institutes can grow into modern, competency-driven capacity building institutions under Mission Karmayogi.
The workshop will be inaugurated by the Hon'ble Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Shri Yogi Adityanath, in the august presence of Dr Jitendra Singh, Hon'ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister's Office and the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.
A Regional Series with a National Purpose
Sādhana Śhrinkhla, short for Strengthening Adaptive Development and Humane Aptitude for National Advancement, is a series of four regional consultative workshops. It carries forward the conversation on institutional reform that the Commission has led over the past year through Regional Task Force meetings, Sādhana Saptah from 2 to 8 April 2026, and the National Departmental Summit on Institutionalising Capacity Building in May 2026.
The series opened at Vijayawada on 29 and 30 September 2026, followed by the North Eastern Region workshop at Guwahati on 9 October 2026. Lucknow now takes the dialogue to the Northern Region.
Participating States and Union Territories
Hosted by the Government of Uttar Pradesh, the workshop will see participation from the States of Bihar, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttarakhand, and the Union Territories of Chandigarh, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Ladakh. Senior State officials will be joined by heads and faculty of Training Institutes, subject experts and industry partners.
With eight States and four Union Territories spanning the Himalayan region, the Indo-Gangetic plains and the desert State of Rajasthan, the Lucknow workshop brings together the widest range of administrative contexts in the series so far.
What the Workshop Will Address
Civil servants today are expected to keep pace with new technologies, changing citizen expectations and complex development priorities. Training Institutes are central to preparing them for this, and the workshop will focus on how they can respond more closely to what officials actually need in their roles.
Deliberations will cover four broad areas: institutional governance and leadership; operational effectiveness and collaboration between institutes; faculty and institutional competencies; and digital transformation, including the use of Artificial Intelligence in training. Each participating State and Union Territory will be supported in identifying its own priorities and drawing up a practical roadmap for reform.
UNNATI as the Common Platform
These reforms will be taken forward through the Unified New-Age National Training Initiatives (UNNATI) portal, launched during Sādhana Saptah 2026. UNNATI connects more than 700 Training Institutes on a single platform and links them to the competency needs identified in Capacity Building Plans, helping institutes share resources, collaborate and improve on the basis of data.
Shaping the Training Institute Transformation Framework
The outcomes of the Lucknow workshop, together with those from Vijayawada, Guwahati and the final regional workshop, will feed into the Training Institute Transformation Framework being developed by the Commission. The Framework will offer a common direction for reform while leaving room for each State's institutional realities.
Through Sādhana Śhrinkhla, the Commission aims to build a connected and responsive network of Training Institutes that equips civil servants to serve citizens better, in keeping with the vision of Mission Karmayogi and Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: NHAI Introduces Independent Checking of Designs of Major Bridges and Critical National Highway Structures
subtitle: Initiative to introduce a uniform mechanism to improve safety, quality and durability of critical structures on National Highways
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 5:02PM by PIB Delhi
content:
To strengthen structural safety, durability and quality assurance of the National Highway projects, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI
)
has introduced a uniform system for independent checking of designs and drawings of major bridges and other critical structures being built under its projects. Under the new policy, the designs of identified critical structures will be independently checked by empanelled Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs), reputed government technical institutions and other experienced technical firms having expertise in bridge engineering and hydraulic studies.
The initiative is particularly important for major bridges and other complex structures. Independent checking will help identify possible design-related issues at an early stage and ensure that structures meet the applicable Indian Roads Congress (IRC) codes, technical specifications and contractual requirements.
Structures to be covered
The policy covers major bridges and viaducts, including major river bridges with a design discharge of 3,000 cubic metres per second or more, and structures or bridges having an individual effective span of 40 metres or more. Other special or complex structures identified by NHAI will also be covered.
The independent checking will include structural design calculations, structural analysis, design drawings and, wherever applicable, hydrological and hydraulic studies. These studies help assess water flow, flood levels, the adequacy of openings for water to pass through and the safety of foundations against river-bed erosion.
How will the new system work?
Under the revised procedure, the contractor or concessionaire will submit the design and drawings for review or approval, as applicable under the contract. Thereafter, three institutions or firms will be proposed from NHAI’s empanelled list. Based on project requirements, one or more institutions or firms will be selected to carry out independent verification.
The selected institution or firm will independently examine the design and submit its observations and recommendations. The contractor or concessionaire will consider these observations and make the necessary changes in the design, as required. The design will then be reviewed or approved by NHAI in accordance with the applicable contractual provisions.
The policy will come into effect from 1st December 2026. It will apply to all new Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC), Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) and Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) National Highway projects, as well as projects where design verification or proof checking has not yet commenced.
The policy will generally not apply to projects where design verification or proof checking has already been completed. However, additional independent verification may be undertaken for major bridges and complex or critical special structures.
Through this initiative, NHAI aims to establish a consistent and robust quality-assurance mechanism for critical National Highway structures that will support development of a safer and stronger National Highway infrastructure across the country.

title: From Lab to Land, Idea to Impact: Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh Urges Industry to Become a Co-Creator in India’s Technology Journey
subtitle:
Research Philanthropy Is as Good as Worship; Investment in Science Can Help Save Lives and Build a Self-Reliant India: Dr. Jitendra Singh

At 'IITK Samanvay 2026', Union Minister Calls for Greater Domestic and International Investment in Deep Technologies

India Must Lead the Next Industrial Revolution Through AI, Quantum and Biotechnology, Says Dr. Jitendra Singh

Scientific Self-Reliance Will Shape India’s Geopolitical Sovereignty and Global Standing on the Road to Viksit Bharat 2047
date:

content:
Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science & Technology and Earth Sciences, and Minister of State in the Prime Minister’s Office, Personnel, Public Grievances, Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, today urged industry to become a co-creator in India’s technology journey, working with researchers from the conception of projects through development, scale-up and commercialisation.
Addressing the third edition of IITK Samanvay 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, he called for greater domestic and international investment in deep technologies and a stronger culture of research philanthropy, describing scientific research as “as good as worship” for its potential to save lives and contribute to national development.
Organised by the Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (IIT Kanpur) under the theme “Emerging Technologies, Enduring Partnerships,” IITK Samanvay 2026 brought together stakeholders from government, industry, academia, startups and research institutions to strengthen collaboration and accelerate the translation of research into market-ready technologies and societal solutions. Prof. Amey Karkare, Dean of Resources & Alumni, IIT Kanpur; Prof. Braj Bhushan, Deputy Director, IIT Kanpur; and Prof. Manindra Agrawal, Director, IIT Kanpur, were present on the dais.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said industry must engage with researchers from the earliest stages of a project, helping identify practical applications, develop viable business models and take innovations to scale. Calling for a shift from conventional collaboration to co-creation, he urged industry leaders to help accelerate the journey “from lab to land, from idea to impact, and from prototype to product.”
The Minister said India had abundant scientific talent, creativity and innovation capacity, but translating these strengths into globally competitive technologies required a larger pool of financial resources and stronger industrial participation. He invited industry to work with the government and research institutions to develop commercially viable models for investment in frontier and deep technologies, including through greater domestic and international participation.
Referring to the ₹1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund announced by PM Sh Narendra Modi in November last year, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the initiative was intended to accelerate industry participation in deep-tech development. He also referred to the liberalisation of foreign direct investment in strategic sectors, including nuclear energy, as part of efforts to mobilise resources for India’s technological ambitions.
Dr. Jitendra Singh called for a stronger culture of philanthropy for scientific research, saying that supporting research could make a direct contribution to human welfare. While philanthropy in education and other social causes remained valuable, he said investment in scientific research and clinical trials could also help advance life-saving interventions.
Referring to a recent successful trial related to haemophilia, a disorder associated with deficiency of clotting factor VIII, the Minister said greater philanthropic support could help scientific institutions advance research and medical interventions. He encouraged philanthropists and other stakeholders to recognise research as an important avenue for contributing to society and national development.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India was witnessing a significant transformation in science and technology, supported by an enabling policy environment and a growing emphasis on future-ready initiatives. Unlike earlier industrial revolutions, in which India adopted several technologies after they had advanced elsewhere, the country now had an opportunity to participate in shaping the next phase of technological progress.
With India advancing in artificial intelligence, quantum technologies and biotechnology, the country was moving into areas expected to drive the next industrial revolution, he said, referring also to initiatives such as Genome India.
Citing the opening of the space sector to private participation in 2019–20, the Minister said India’s space startup ecosystem had grown from single-digit numbers to more than 400 startups. He placed the country’s space economy at around USD 9 billion, with projections of reaching USD 45 billion by the end of the decade.
Dr. Jitendra Singh also referred to the growth of India’s startup ecosystem to around 2.5 lakh startups and the expansion of the bio-manufacturing sector from approximately USD 10 billion to nearly USD 200 billion over about a decade. He attributed these developments to policy support, an enabling ecosystem and greater emphasis on innovation and entrepreneurship.
The Minister said the National Research Foundation was an important institutional mechanism for strengthening India’s research ecosystem. Its approach brings together scientific expertise with perspectives from social sciences, humanities and traditional knowledge, broadening the societal relevance of research and its contribution to national priorities.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said India’s long-term development would depend on its ability to build self-reliance through indigenous manufacturing, technology development and the effective use of domestic resources. Scientific and technological self-reliance, he said, would also shape India’s geopolitical sovereignty and its standing in the international arena.
Referring to India’s ambition of achieving 100 GW of nuclear energy capacity by 2047 and net-zero emissions by 2070, the Minister stressed the importance of sustained technological innovation in meeting the country’s long-term development goals.
Dr. Jitendra Singh said platforms such as IITK Samanvay must translate dialogue into enduring partnerships, investment and measurable outcomes. Closer collaboration among government, industry, academia, startups and researchers, supported by sustained investment and a stronger culture of scientific philanthropy, would help accelerate innovation, strengthen indigenous technological capabilities and advance the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

The Nine-day SHILP SAMAGAM MELA 2026, organized by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is continuing at the Mysuru Dasara Exhibition Grounds, in Karnataka since October 11. The Mela will conclude on October 19 Monday.
A Senior Official in the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC) said the Mela provides a marketing platform for artisans and beneficiaries from Scheduled Castes (SCs), Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Safai Karamcharis, enabling them to showcase their traditional handicrafts, handloom products and other goods to a wider audience.
He said the Mela has been jointly organized by three national corporations under the Ministry namely National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC), which provide financial assistance to artisans and eligible beneficiaries.
Union Minister of State of Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale during his visit to SHILP SAMAGAM MELA highlighted the Central Government’s commitment to the economic and social empowerment of socially disadvantaged and vulnerable sections.
The Minister was informed that the ongoing Mela features 83 stalls, including 80 stalls allotted to artisans, among them 37 women artisans. Artisans from 12 States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Kerala, Rajasthan, Puducherry, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh, are participating in the exhibition.
The Minister visited and inspected stalls with a diverse range of products, including handicrafts, handloom sarees, spices, pickles, incense sticks, honey products, block-printed items, leather goods, wooden toys, bags, purses, terracotta products, artificial jewellery, rosewood wall hangings, and bed and cushion covers. He also visited the Food stalls serving traditional delicacies adding to the visitor experience.
Addressing a press conference at the Government Guest House in Mysuru earlier, Shri Athawale said that the Central Government has introduced various welfare and development schemes to promote the economic and social empowerment of Scheduled Castes, Other Backward Classes, sanitation workers, transgender persons and persons with disabilities, including persons with visual impairments. He highlighted the role of the National Development Corporations in extending concessional financial assistance, with loans ranging from ₹1.5 Lakh To ₹35 Lakh under various schemes, subject to applicable eligibility criteria and scheme provisions.
Emphasizing the Government’s commitment to social welfare, the Minister stated that ₹1.98 Lakh Crore had been allocated for social welfare schemes in the Union Budget, out of a total budget of ₹ 57 Lakh Crore.
Shri Athawale also referred to the constitutional provisions for reservation for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, the provision of 27 per cent reservation for Other Backward Classes following the recommendations of the Mandal Commission, and the subsequent introduction of 10 per cent reservation for Economically Weaker Sections.
Highlighting the reach of flagship welfare initiatives, Shri Athawale referred to the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, under which around four crore beneficiaries have received benefits across the country, including approximately 10 lakh beneficiaries in Karnataka. He also highlighted the contribution of the Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana in expanding financial inclusion, stating that 2,22,23,000 bank accounts had been opened in Karnataka under the scheme.
Referring to educational assistance in Mysuru district, the Minister stated that approximately 13,000 students studying in Classes I to VIII and 31,000 post-matric students had benefited from educational support. He further noted that nearly 75 per cent of the 7,000 students residing in 84 government hostels in the district belonged to Scheduled Castes. Eligible beneficiaries were also receiving monthly stipends of ₹1,850 for college students and ₹1,750 for high school students, he said.
The Mela is designed to strengthen market linkages for artisans, promote traditional craftsmanship and create sustainable livelihood opportunities. Through direct interaction with visitors and prospective customers, participating artisans can display their products, expand their customer base and improve the market reach of their enterprises. The initiative also promotes India’s rich cultural heritage and supports the preservation of traditional art forms and skills.
The SHILP SAMAGAM MELA also serves as an important platform for disseminating information about the schemes and programmes of the Ministry and its three national corporations, helping eligible beneficiaries learn about available financial assistance and entrepreneurship opportunities.
The Ministry facilitates artisans’ participation by providing free stalls and support towards travel expenses, daily allowance, transportation of goods and meals, in accordance with the applicable arrangements.
In addition to the Mela, the Ministry is promoting the BHARAT TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) initiative to expand market access for products made by target-group artisans through digital platforms in India and abroad. Branding products under BHARAT TULIP is intended to improve their visibility, facilitate online sales and connect traditional artisans with a wider customer base.
The Ministry has been organizing SHILP SAMAGAM MELAS since 2022, benefiting 975 artisans through 13 fairs held so far.
The ongoing Mysuru edition is the first SHILP SAMAGAM MELA of the financial year 2026–27.
The Ministry also proposes to organize additional fairs in Guwahati, Dilli Haat in New Delhi, Jodhpur and Lucknow during the current financial year, alongside participation in major exhibitions such as the India International Trade Fair 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, from November 14 to 27, 2026, and the Surajkund Mela in February 2027.

title: From Sanitation Worker to Entrepreneur
subtitle: Shiv Lal’s Journey Towards Dignity and Self-Reliance
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                15 OCT 2026 4:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
For nearly two decades, Mr. Shiv Lal, a 44-year-old resident of Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan, worked as a Sewer and Septic Tank Cleaning Helper to support his family.
Belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) Valmiki community, he faced persistent financial challenges despite years of hard work and dedication. Having studied only up to the 8th standard, he had limited opportunities to acquire technical skills or secure better-paying employment. His monthly income of approximately Rs 6,000 was insufficient to meet household expenses and provide adequately for his children’s education.
Mr. Shiv Lal married in 2002, and his wife is a homemaker. His 19-year-old son recently gained admission to college, while his 10-year-old daughter continues her schooling. With limited financial resources, meeting daily household needs and supporting his children’s educational aspirations remained a constant challenge. Nevertheless, he remained determined to improve his family’s circumstances and create a more secure future for his children.
Despite working in the sanitation sector for many years, Mr. Shiv Lal had limited opportunities for economic advancement. His modest earnings, lack of technical skills and limited educational qualifications restricted his ability to become financially independent. Social stigma and discrimination associated with sanitation work presented additional challenges. However, he aspired to move beyond daily-wage employment and establish a business of his own. He envisioned purchasing a Tractor cum Suction Machine that would enable him to provide sanitation services independently, earn a better income and improve his family’s quality of life.
A significant turning point came on 12 August 2025, when Mr. Shiv Lal received financial assistance under the Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY), a component of the NAMASTE Scheme. The assistance, provided through an upfront capital subsidy, helped him procure a Tractor cum Suction Machine and establish his own sanitation service business. The total project cost was Rs 11,34,000, of which Rs 7,25,500 was financed through a loan and Rs 4,08,500 was provided as a capital subsidy. This support helped him overcome a major financial barrier and transition from working as a helper to becoming a self-employed entrepreneur.
Today, Mr. Shiv Lal operates his own sanitation service business, giving him greater control over his livelihood and improved earning opportunities. After meeting his monthly loan repayment of approximately Rs 18,186 and labour expenses of around Rs 8,000, he reports a net monthly surplus of approximately Rs 10,000–Rs 12,000 after accounting for operational expenses and repayments. Compared with his earlier monthly income of Rs 6,000, this represents a meaningful improvement in his economic circumstances and earning potential.
The intervention has also strengthened Mr. Shiv Lal’s confidence and enabled him to pursue his aspiration of building a sustainable livelihood. His improved financial position provides greater support for his children’s education and his family’s needs. By becoming a business owner, he has taken an important step towards self-reliance and greater dignity in his professional life.
Mr. Shiv Lal’s journey demonstrates how targeted financial assistance and access to productive assets can create opportunities for sanitation workers to become entrepreneurs. Through the Swachhta Udyami Yojana under the NAMASTE Scheme, he has been able to move beyond low-paid employment and establish an independent source of livelihood. His experience reflects the importance of inclusive development initiatives that empower sanitation workers, promote economic independence and support families in building a more secure future.
From a modest monthly wage to an independent sanitation enterprise, Mr. Shiv Lal’s journey is a testament to perseverance, opportunity and the pursuit of dignity through self-reliance.

Timely access to counselling, medical care and rehabilitation definitely help individuals overcome substance dependence and rebuild their lives.
Mr. Rajesh Kumar’s journey reflects the importance of institutional support and structured rehabilitation in helping individuals recover from alcohol addiction, restore their confidence and work towards a stable and dignified life.
Rajesh Kumar
(name changed)
, a 47-year-old self-employed individual from Dhenkanal district of Odisha, had been struggling with alcohol addiction for nearly 23 years. His prolonged dependence on alcohol adversely affected his personal life, family relationships and professional responsibilities. Frequent conflicts and emotional distress strained his marriage, eventually resulting in separation from his wife.
Despite working in the catering profession and earning approximately ₹10,000 per month, he found it difficult to overcome his addiction independently. Limited financial resources, social stigma and isolation further compounded his challenges. Nevertheless, he remained determined to regain his self-confidence, restore his dignity and resume his professional responsibilities.
The meeting with a social worker associated with ASHRA–Integrated Rehabilitation Centre for Addicts (IRCA), functioning under the Arun Institute of Rural Affairs in Dhenkanal, proved a turning point for Mr Kumar. This worker identified his condition and facilitated his admission to the rehabilitation centre.
With the support under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR), Mr. Rajesh received structured rehabilitation services to help him overcome alcohol dependence and rebuild his life. During his one-month residential stay, he received detoxification services, individual counselling, psychological and emotional support, behavioural therapy and motivational guidance. The centre provided a safe and supportive environment, along with basic care and assistance to help him regain self-control and develop a positive outlook towards life.
The rehabilitation programme helped Mr. Rajesh understand the importance of maintaining sobriety and working towards emotional stability and social reintegration.
Following the completion of rehabilitation, he resumed his catering profession with renewed confidence and a greater sense of responsibility. His monthly income increased from approximately ₹10,000 to ₹16,000, reflecting improved work consistency and livelihood stability. The intervention also supported his efforts to become more self-reliant and move towards a healthier and more productive life.
Today, Mr. Rajesh’s journey demonstrates how accessible rehabilitation, professional counselling and sustained motivational support can help individuals overcome the challenges associated with substance dependence. The timely assistance provided through ASHRA–IRCA under the NAPDDR scheme enabled him to take meaningful steps towards recovery, livelihood improvement and social reintegration. His experience highlights the importance of community outreach, compassionate care and institutional support in helping individuals rebuild their lives with dignity and renewed hope.
Mr. Rajesh’s story stands as an example of determination and the transformative potential of rehabilitation support. It underscores the importance of providing individuals affected by addiction with appropriate care and opportunities to regain their confidence, strengthen their livelihoods and work towards a stable, productive and self-reliant future.
